title: Interpretable machine learning maps wastewater treatment conditions
summary: An XGBoost model fitted to 1,423 experimental and literature-derived samples linked iron/carbon ratio and operating conditions to chemical oxygen demand removal in polyvinyl-alcohol wastewater treatment. SHAP analysis identified iron/carbon ratio as the strongest modeled factor and a pH-dependent interaction window. Reported test R² was 0.8045, but the paper selected its final model using that test set, limiting an unbiased generalization claim. The preprint offers model-derived process associations, not a confirmed causal mechanism or validated industrial-scale control policy.

tested: Seven-model comparison on a mixed 1,423-sample dataset; interpretation of Fe/C ratio, pH and other process conditions.
unknown: Model selection used the held-out test set; literature/source dependence, causal interpretation, real-effluent transfer and industrial-scale outcomes are unresolved.

title: Learned lesion-network models identify shared and specific stroke cognition patterns
summary: A November 24, 2026 preprint analyzed 3,034 patients across 13 stroke cohorts using learned models of lesion anatomy, network connectivity and clinical characteristics. Structural lesion connectivity supplied most of the gain beyond clinical information and infarct size, with left anterior thalamic connectivity consistently informative across cognitive outcomes. Benefits persisted for several outcomes when entire cohorts were held out. The results support a bounded lesion-in-context account of cognitive impairment, without establishing causal circuitry or clinical readiness.
ai_technology: Stacked ridge classifiers and regularized logistic meta-learner; interpretable feature ablation and cross-cohort prediction
organization: University Medical Center Utrecht; Meta VCI Map consortium; Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf; Research Centre Jülich
tested: Nested repeated cross-validation evaluated 3,034 patients from 13 cohorts. Adding anatomy and connectivity improved six of seven targets; any-domain impairment AUPRC rose from 0.67 to 0.71. Leave-one-cohort-out tests retained significant gains for three of seven targets by normalized AUPRC. Stable model coefficients highlighted shared thalamic connectivity and domain-specific anatomical profiles.
unknown: Retrospective pooled cohorts were heterogeneous and predominantly represented mild strokes and Asian or European ancestry. Cognitive outcomes were binary at one assessment within a year, with premorbid cognition unavailable. Cross-cohort performance varied and several domain gains did not transfer significantly. Prediction and coefficient stability do not prove causation or clinical utility.
ai_role: Ridge base classifiers learned complementary lesion representations and a logistic stacking model combined out-of-fold predictions. Ablation, stable coefficients and unseen-cohort tests linked predictive gains to specific network anatomy rather than lesion volume alone.

title: Machine learning links multidomain profiles to fall history
summary: In a cross-sectional study of 147 community-dwelling adults aged 55 and older, machine-learning models classified ordered past-year fall-history groups from physical-function, activity, health and social measures. Random Forest reported four-class accuracy of 0.946 and binary AUC of 0.968 under internal five-fold validation after excluding fall-location, fall-situation and fear-of-falling variables. The preprint describes associations with recorded fall history, not prediction of future falls. A small, imbalanced single-region sample and self-reported measures limit generalization; external and prospective validation remain necessary.

organization: Shahid Bahonar University of Kerman; University of Saskatchewan; Sport Science Research Institute

unknown: Cross-sectional history, self-report and small uneven strata; no external validation, causal effects or demonstrated future-fall prediction.

title: GPT-6.2 protein designs show binding across five targets in laboratory tests
summary: OpenAI reports that Onava laboratory tests found binding for 35 of 322 minibinders based on GPT-6.2-designed structures, with at least one hit for each of five targets. GPT-6.2 generated backbone designs using reasoning and general-purpose code, while SolubleMPNN supplied sequences and specialized models helped select candidates. The November 24, 2026 announcement links a preprint; the findings do not establish an end-to-end workflow without specialized models, independent replication, specificity, therapeutic activity or clinical benefit.

organization: OpenAI; Onava

title: Generative models guide ribozymes that retain activity at high temperature
summary: A November 24, 2026 preprint reports laboratory-tested catalytic RNA designs that remain active at 60°C. A learned evolutionary sequence model combined with an independent RNA thermodynamic score generated variants that preserved function more often than either score alone. Across 2,500 designed variants from ten starting sequences, the jointly favored group had a 72.5% high-temperature activity hit rate, compared with 7.8% for the evolutionary-score group and 0.4% for the physical-score group. The result is limited to one ribozyme family and the study’s assay.
ai_technology: Edge-activation direct coupling analysis (DCA); learned Potts sequence model combined with RNA thermodynamics
organization: Sorbonne Université; CNRS; ESPCI Paris; Institut Polytechnique de Paris; Sapienza University of Rome
tested: Laboratory activity measurements compared 1,500 jointly favored designs with 500 evolutionary-score and 500 physical-score designs, pooled across ten starting sequences. High-temperature activity hit rates were 72.5%, 7.8% and 0.4%, respectively, under the study’s reference-normalized threshold.
unknown: The study examines one self-splicing RNA family and uses a pooled enrichment assay rather than general application performance. Molecular dynamics provides mechanistic interpretation, not independent experimental confirmation of the proposed structural explanation. Independent replication and transfer to other families remain unestablished.
ai_role: An edge-activation DCA model learned family-specific sequence constraints from an alignment of 817 natural sequences. Combining its generative prior with a separately derived thermodynamic score guided designs whose catalytic activity was then measured.

title: AI-designed visual stimuli probe how perceptual learning changes decisions
summary: A November 24, 2026 preprint used the learned DorsalNet visual model to design motion stimuli targeting different model stages, then tested training in 19 human observers. After three days, ten observers trained on late-stage stimuli showed increased perceptual sensitivity, while nine trained on early-stage stimuli mainly changed response bias. Transfer tests and model comparisons were consistent with a late-stage readout account. Cortical stages were not directly recorded, and separate participant groups limit causal comparison.
ai_technology: DorsalNet; learned neural visual model and gradient-based stimulus synthesis
organization: McGill University; Université de Montréal; Mila
tested: Nineteen observers trained for three days. Late-stage-group sensitivity increased (n=10; paired p=0.001); early-stage-group change was not significant (n=9; p=0.100), while its response criterion changed. Transfer across location and stimulus type informed comparisons with alternative model readouts.
unknown: A difference in within-group significance does not itself prove a between-group learning interaction. Separate groups may differ before training; stimulus-to-cortical-stage correspondence was inferred from the model rather than directly measured. Model–human specificity agreement was assessed qualitatively, and energetic interpretations remain speculative.
ai_role: DorsalNet, trained on self-motion from naturalistic videos, enabled stimulus synthesis selectively separating early or late model-layer responses. Human tests supplied new behavioral evidence relevant to competing perceptual-learning accounts.

title: Epigenetic deep learning detects a lifestyle-trial signature
summary: CheekAI neural networks trained on 25,400 buccal methylation profiles from 14,716 adults were applied retrospectively to external datasets. In an existing eight-week randomized lifestyle trial with 18 intervention and 20 control participants, the model’s age-adjusted score decreased by 1.34 model-years relative to controls (p = 0.021), largely through dietary and metabolic proxy components. This preprint reports a learned methylation-score response, not demonstrated reversal of biological aging or improved health. The score was designed to reflect lifestyle proxies; a separate semaglutide analysis did not significantly reduce the overall score and showed tissue-transfer limitations.

organization: Tally Health; University of California, San Diego; TruDiagnostic
tested: Person-grouped nested cross-validation, replicate testing and retrospective analysis of existing intervention/control and external methylation datasets.
unknown: Lifestyle-weighted score is not a validated biological-aging or health-benefit endpoint; small external trial, tissue transfer and proxy interpretation limit inference.
ai_role: Neural networks predict age and epigenetic lifestyle/health biomarker proxies from methylation principal components; a learned additive combination enables interpretable retrospective response analysis.

title: Learned cell-shape signatures predict confined transit
summary: Support-vector and logistic classifiers linked cell area and circularity to whether MDA-MB-231 breast-cancer cells would traverse microfluidic constrictions. Less circular cells were more likely to transit, and trajectory features about 30 minutes before an event were most informative. Models transferred without retraining to narrower constrictions and more adhesive surfaces. This preprint reports a condition-dependent association in one cell line, not a causal mechanism or a predictor of metastasis in patients.

title: Learned brain-activity profiles guide tested drug leads in zebrafish models
summary: A November 24, 2026 preprint combined large-scale zebrafish brain imaging, learned clustering and random-forest ranking to select drug conditions for follow-up. Several candidates improved movement in larval toxin models and preserved dopamine-neuron reporter signals under some conditions. These are preliminary, compound- and model-dependent findings rather than evidence of Parkinson’s disease treatment in people. Some screened conditions were toxic, and retained fluorescence does not by itself establish prevention of neuronal death.
ai_technology: CNSDIP; consensus clustering and random-forest ranking of brain-activity maps
organization: Sun Yat-sen University; Guangdong Pharmaceutical University; East China Normal University
tested: Sixteen top-ranked conditions underwent follow-up; after toxicity exclusions, five compounds and one pair improved movement in tested conditions. Behavioral comparisons used n=10 and dopamine-reporter cell-count comparisons n=5. Blinded imaging counts supported preservation of identifiable reporter-positive cells for some candidates across three larval toxin models.
unknown: The assays are small and preclinical; not every candidate worked across every model or outcome. Five conditions showed long-term toxicity. Reporter loss or preservation can reflect neuronal phenotype rather than irreversible death or true neuroprotection. Known drug mechanisms explain some effects, and neither efficacy nor safety in people is established.
ai_role: Consensus clustering linked drug-induced brain-activity patterns to a therapeutic reference class; a random forest trained on 363 CNS/non-CNS drugs then ranked candidates for new behavioral and cellular tests. The measured follow-up, rather than classifier accuracy alone, is the admitted result.

title: Bivexia selects an interaction-selective LAG-3 inhibitor tested in mouse models
summary: A November 24, 2026 bioRxiv preprint reports that Bivexia used random-forest predictions of four protein-interaction assays to select BVX-01, a small molecule that disrupted LAG-3 interactions with tau and amyloid-beta while preserving two other tested interactions. The authors report nanomolar LAG-3 binding, activity in donor-derived neurons, and reduced pathology readouts in two mouse models, with two cohorts per model. This is preclinical evidence from the discovery study, not peer-reviewed or independent confirmation or evidence of clinical benefit; the full cascade rests on one compound, and broader target campaigns stopped at primary screening.

organization: Columbia University Irving Medical Center

title: Unsupervised program learning links a beta-cell signature to insulin secretion
summary: A November 24, 2026 preprint used donor-resolved non-negative matrix factorization and consensus program discovery to identify a beta-cell gene program reduced in type 2 diabetes. Learned program definitions were fixed before testing in other datasets. Higher program scores were associated with greater stimulated insulin release in donor-matched measurements from two laboratories. The laboratories shared most donors, so these are complementary measurements rather than independent biological replications, and the association does not establish a causal mechanism or treatment target.
ai_technology: Donor-resolved non-smooth non-negative matrix factorization; cross-donor consensus gene-program discovery
organization: Jinggangshan University; The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Shenzhen University of Advanced Technology; Shenzhen People’s Hospital
tested: Program discovery used 48 donors. Primary independent single-cell validation used 55 eligible HPAP donors, with additional pooled Smart-seq2 and bulk analyses. Functional associations used 52 UPenn and 42 Vanderbilt donors, of whom 39 overlapped; higher frozen program scores tracked stimulated insulin release after diagnosis and preparation-quality adjustments.
unknown: Existing-data associations are retrospective and do not establish that the program causes secretory dysfunction. Two laboratories largely measured the same donors; bulk cell-composition adjustment was not robust across platforms. Patient-level clinical utility, causal perturbation and independent biological replication remain unestablished.
ai_role: NMF learned additive gene-expression programs separately in donor/cell-type units; cross-donor consensus construction identified recurring programs before outcome testing. This learned program discovery, rather than visualization or dimensionality reduction alone, enabled the fixed beta-cell signature and its subsequent functional association tests.

title: Learned receptor networks guide an experimentally tested AT1R modulator
summary: A November 24, 2026 preprint reports that learned Bayesian networks of receptor dynamics helped prioritize an intracellular region of the angiotensin II type 1 receptor for compound screening. Laboratory signaling, radioligand and mutational tests supported a proposed negative allosteric effect of the resulting low-affinity fragment Q2. The experiments establish a bounded cellular pharmacology finding; they do not directly resolve the fragment’s binding pose or demonstrate therapeutic efficacy.
ai_technology: Interpretable Bayesian network structure learning from molecular-dynamics interaction-energy time series
organization: City of Hope; McGill University
tested: Screening of nine prioritized compounds identified Q2. Cellular signaling and radioligand assays, repeated in at least three experiments for key comparisons, showed altered agonist responses. Receptor mutations and G-protein-knockout tests supported the proposed allosteric interpretation; a six-receptor panel showed preferential, incomplete selectivity.

Bootstrap stability was conditional on fixed inferred network topology. Generalization, independent replication, safety and therapeutic efficacy remain unestablished.

summary: A pretrained convolutional network separated tissue compartments in an optoacoustic imaging study of 46 healthy volunteers spanning six Fitzpatrick skin types. Across 3,016 scans and 41 wavelengths, superficial skin signals showed stronger pigmentation associations and unreliable oxygenation responses, while deeper muscle signals responded more clearly to physiological challenges. title: Action-trained models reveal a hand–tool representational link in macaque cortex
summary: A November 24, 2026 preprint compared learned visual representations with macaque brain responses to static images. A Video Swin Transformer trained on fine-grained hand–object interactions matched parietal and prefrontal hand–tool geometry better than static-object and general-action models. Functional ultrasound in two other monkeys independently supported spatial alignment of tool and human-hand responses. The findings concern representational similarity; they do not establish that interaction experience caused the cortical organization or that monkeys understand tool functions.
ai_technology: Video Swin Transformer trained on Something-Something V2; CORnet-S and Kinetics-400 model comparisons
organization: KU Leuven; VIB; NeuroSpin; University of Trento; Massachusetts General Hospital
tested: Whole-brain fMRI used 121 runs across three macaques; functional ultrasound sampled parietal cortex in two separate macaques. Learned category representations from four model stages or training conditions were compared with neural geometry. The interaction-trained model retained positive associations in several parietal and prefrontal regions after controlling other models and checking predictor sensitivity.
unknown: Only five animals and static stimuli were studied. Model geometries were highly correlated, with variance inflation factors of 6.40–11.71. Shape, posture, affordance and dataset statistics remain possible contributors. Similarity does not establish computational equivalence, evolutionary history or a causal effect of observing human tool use.
ai_role: Pretrained networks transformed identical images into learned feature vectors and category dissimilarity matrices. Comparing the same Video Swin architecture trained on broad actions versus fine-grained hand–object interactions enabled the specific finding that interaction-oriented learned geometry better corresponded to dorsal cortical representations.

title: Multimodal AI finds lung-cancer tissue signatures associated with survival
summary: A November 23, 2026 preprint reports that VirTues-M2 learned joint tissue morphology and spatial-protein representations to discover survival-associated cellular signatures in lung cancer. Signatures selected on 737 patients stratified survival in 316 held-out patients and transferred without retraining to a separate 39-patient cohort. Low-risk signatures marked organized immune-rich neighborhoods; high-risk signatures marked more disorganized tumor-rich tissue. These are retrospective prognostic associations with small external validation and no demonstrated treatment benefit.
ai_technology: VirTues-M2; multimodal vision transformer and learned cell-signature transfer
organization: EPFL; University Hospital Zurich; University of Zurich; University of Bern
tested: Signature selection used 737 discovery patients and evaluation used 316 held-out patients. Combined signatures reached C-index 0.646 and hazard ratio 3.09 in the test set. Unchanged signature classifiers transferred to 39 external patients; combined signatures had C-index 0.636 and hazard ratio 2.87 (p=0.039).

Test patients used pre-specified tertiles, whereas external patients used a median split. Prospective clinical utility and robustness require further evaluation.
ai_role: A marker-aware multimodal transformer learned joint H&E and spatial-proteomics representations. Clustering enabled annotation-free cell-state discovery; Cox screening selected survival-linked populations and random-forest classifiers transferred their membership to another cohort.

title: Learned MRI models link cord motion and compression level to myelopathy severity
summary: A November 23, 2026 study analyzed MRI measurements from 112 patients with degenerative cervical myelopathy. Learned hierarchical classifiers identified compression at C3/4 as a severity-associated feature. In the larger training subgroup with compression elsewhere, adding spinal cord motion improved cross-validated severity classification accuracy from 69.6% to 73.7%. Internal testing on 22 patients produced one additional correct classification. This single-center result supports a limited diagnostic association, without establishing causation, future disease progression or treatment benefit.
ai_technology: Decision trees, support-vector machines and kernel logistic regression; Bayesian hyperparameter optimization
organization: Balgrist University Hospital; University of Zurich
tested: A 90-patient training set and 22-patient internal test set were formed from 112 patients. The 15-patient C3/4 training subgroup was too small for the motion-feature comparison. title: Graph-learning-guided tests identify functionally important enzyme positions
summary: A November 23, 2026 preprint used SCOPE, a learned structural-graph model, to prioritize enzyme positions for laboratory tests. Across four low-homology enzymes, substitutions at 11 selected positions left 0–4.1% of reference activity. The tested set included established sites and additional predicted positions, so the result is a bounded functional map rather than 11 newly discovered catalytic residues. Activity loss supports functional importance but can reflect stability or structural effects instead of direct reaction chemistry.
ai_technology: SCOPE DeepGCN structural-graph learning with ProtT5 sequence embeddings and a Gaussian auxiliary training objective
organization: Northwest A&F University; Adelaide University; Monash University; Beijing University of Chemical Technology
tested: Model-prioritized positions were tested in four enzymes using activity assays with three independent experiments and reference-enzyme normalization. Eleven tested positions had 0–4.1% residual activity; protein expression was checked. Two tested copper-coordinating sites were explicitly already established, while other model-selected positions included active-pocket and distal contexts.

Selection of the tested sites using SCOPE makes relative-model comparisons descriptive, not unbiased. Known-site recovery is not counted as a new discovery, and independent replication or broad applicability remains unestablished.
ai_role: Deep graph learning combined residue-level structure, evolutionary information and protein-language-model embeddings to rank candidate functional positions. These rankings guided new functional tests, linking the learned operation to measured enzyme activity rather than only benchmark performance.

title: Satellite machine learning maps vegetation change near a highway
summary: Random Forest classification of fused Sentinel optical and radar observations mapped land-cover change along a section of India’s National Highway 344 from 2016 to 2021. title: MAPLE matches reference diagnoses in a small breast-pathology slide cohort
summary: A November 23, 2026 bioRxiv preprint reports that MAPLE, a hierarchical pathology vision-language system, matched expert reference diagnoses for 15 breast whole-slide images from Johns Hopkins at both 20x and 40x magnification. The series comprised nine invasive carcinoma, three ductal carcinoma in situ and three benign cases; the system combined learned nucleus-based region selection, a pathology CLIP encoder and a Qwen3-14B-based language model. This small, single-institution retrospective test is not evidence of prospective diagnostic benefit or readiness for routine deployment; the paper also reports separate benchmark results.

title: AI-designed enhancers control gene expression in healthy mammalian cells
summary: CRG researchers measured more than 64,000 synthetic enhancers across seven stages of blood-cell development and found that enhancer combinations can activate genes in one cell type but repress them in another. summary: A genome-informed machine-learning workflow (ML-CITO) used contrastive learning over protein-language-model representations and genomic context, starting from 14 known phenazine-modifying sequences, to identify PTC. title: DefensePredictor uncovers dozens of previously unknown bacterial anti-phage systems
summary: DefensePredictor, a machine-learning classifier using protein-language-model embeddings, nominated candidate defense genes across diverse E. coli strains. title: Interpretable multi-omics machine learning reveals unexpected drug mechanisms in Huntington disease models
summary: An interpretable machine-learning model integrated transcriptomic, epigenomic, metabolomic and proteomic data from Huntington-disease cell models to identify previously unknown mechanisms for protective compounds. title: LIGHTHOUSE identifies riboflavin 5′-monophosphate as a PPAT inhibitor
summary: LIGHTHOUSE, a deep-learning model using protein sequence and chemical representations, nominated riboflavin 5′-monophosphate as an inhibitor of PPAT, a target without reported inhibitors in the paper. title: deepDTnet repurposes topotecan as an RORγt inhibitor for multiple-sclerosis models
summary: The deep-learning network deepDTnet predicted retinoic-acid-receptor-related orphan receptor gamma-t (RORγt) as a previously unrecognized target of topotecan. title: CLEAN experimentally identifies SAM hydrolase activity in previously uncharacterized proteins
summary: Researchers at the University of Illinois Urbana–Champaign developed CLEAN, a contrastive-learning enzyme-function predictor, and used it to identify the SAM hydrolase activity of the previously uncharacterized protein TTHA0338. title: deepAMP designs broad-spectrum antimicrobial peptides active against resistant bacteria
summary: Researchers at Hunan University and collaborators used the peptide language model deepAMP to optimize antimicrobial peptides and experimentally tested 29 candidates. summary: The team used AlphaFold2 structure predictions to cluster the deaminase family and found that most proteins in a DddA-like clade were not double-stranded DNA deaminases. title: CataPro-assisted enzyme mining identifies a high-activity Sphingobium enzyme for vanillin production
summary: CataPro, a deep-learning model using pretrained protein-language representations and molecular fingerprints to predict enzyme kinetics, was combined with sequence and structure-based filtering to screen candidate enzymes for converting 4-vinylguaiacol to vanillin. The team experimentally identified Sphingobium sp. organization: Shandong University; Shanghai Zelixir Biotech; Shenzhen Institute of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences

summary: An image-classification-guided pooled CRISPRi screen mapped factors that affect TFEB movement from nucleus to cytosol during prolonged starvation. summary: Researchers iteratively combined sequence mining, machine-learning activity/property predictors and high-throughput assays to screen natural enzyme homologs. summary: The OSMES workflow screened AlphaFold-modeled vitamin-B6-dependent enzymes by docking the substrate into active sites and ranking catalytically favorable conformations. summary: A hybrid workflow coupled machine-learning models with enzyme-treated peptide arrays to predict previously unexplored protein post-translational-modification sites. summary: DeepMet, an LSTM chemical language model trained on known human metabolites, generated a ranked space of metabolite-like structures and was integrated with mass spectrometry data. summary: A deep-learning system called MitoReID classified drug mechanisms from time-resolved mitochondrial morphology and membrane-potential images. title: EnzySFC discovers nitrile-hydratase activity in nitrilases and evolves amide-selective variants
summary: The AI-assisted EnzySFC workflow experimentally validated 10 previously uncharacterized nitrilases selected from 1,113 candidates. A wild-type Phototrophicales nitrilase showed exclusive nitrile hydratase activity; a separate Actinomycetia nitrilase was AI-evolved, with four tested top variants reaching 100% amide yield and complete substrate conversion.
ai_technology: EnzySFC AI-assisted enzyme discovery and functional-evolution platform
organization: China State Institute of Pharmaceutical Industry, Research Center for Systems Biosynthesis
tested: The AI-assisted EnzySFC workflow experimentally validated 10 previously uncharacterized nitrilases selected from 1,113 candidates.
unknown: The reported outcomes are enzyme and substrate assays; the abstract does not establish industrial scale performance or application in a living system. The 10 discovery candidates and 16 mutants were experimental follow-ups to model prioritization, not comprehensive validation of all 1,113 sequences.
ai_role: EnzySFC combined de novo enzyme discovery and multiobjective activity/specificity optimization to rank candidate nitrilases and propose evolved mutants. The study experimentally tested ten discovery candidates and sixteen mutants from one evolution prediction cycle; the named activity switch and product-selective variants were measured in assays.
source_review: null

title: Machine-learning metabolomics identifies widespread promiscuous activities in Escherichia coli enzymes
summary: In vitro metabolomics of 667 purified E. coli enzymes, analyzed with a machine-learning-derived multivariate classifier, indicated previously unrecognized promiscuous activities in 11% of enzymes tested. Follow-up reconstruction assigned 22 reaction stoichiometries to 11 enzymes, with four reactions experimentally validated; examples include expanded nucleotide-substrate use by DeoA, cofactor and sugar promiscuity in NanK, and FMN dephosphorylation by CobC. Follow-up assays also found that pyrimidine-specific ribonucleoside hydrolase RihB acted on thymidine, guanosine and deoxyuridine, further extending its measured substrate range.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-derived multivariate classifier applied to enzyme metabolomics ion-trace data
organization: ETH Zurich; Weizmann Institute of Science; University Children’s Hospital Zurich and University of Zurich
tested: In vitro metabolomics of 667 purified E. coli enzymes, analyzed with a machine-learning-derived multivariate classifier, indicated previously unrecognized promiscuous activities in 11% of enzymes tested.
unknown: The classifier operated at a 33% false-discovery rate; the 135 ion traces were putatively annotated, and only four of 22 reconstructed reaction stoichiometries were experimentally validated. Therefore the full 11% result is a set of candidate activities, not 11% independently confirmed enzyme functions. The RihB activities were prompted by a low-confidence potassium-thymidine-adduct trace and then tested directly with purified enzyme; they should be distinguished from the classifier’s higher-confidence hit set.
ai_role: A machine-learning-derived multivariate classifier, with a reported false-discovery rate of 33%, detected unexpected changes in metabolite ion traces in the enzyme assays and helped nominate candidate promiscuous activities. The researchers then reconstructed candidate reaction stoichiometries and experimentally validated four reactions.
source_review: null

title: Generative deep learning discovers the RIPK1 inhibitor RI-962 with an unreported scaffold
summary: A target-conditioned generative deep-learning model based on a distribution-learning conditional recurrent neural network generated a tailored compound library that was screened for RIPK1 inhibition. The study reports RI-962 as a potent inhibitor with a previously unreported scaffold, validated in vitro for protection from necroptosis and in vivo in two inflammatory models.
ai_technology: Generative deep-learning distribution-learning conditional recurrent neural network (GDL cRNN)
organization: State Key Laboratory of Biotherapy and Cancer Center, West China Hospital, Sichuan University; West China School of Pharmacy, Sichuan University
tested: The study reports RI-962 as a potent inhibitor with a previously unreported scaffold, validated in vitro for protection from necroptosis and in vivo in two inflammatory models.
unknown: Evidence is preclinical: cellular necroptosis assays and two inflammatory mouse models do not establish human efficacy or safety. The paper identifies one leading molecule from a generated library; it does not validate generative-model performance across targets generally.
ai_role: The GDL cRNN generated a target-tailored virtual compound library; virtual screening and subsequent chemical synthesis and bioactivity assays selected RI-962. This provides direct experimental testing of a model-generated molecule rather than a prediction-only hit.
source_review: null

title: Machine-learning-guided screening identifies Bcl-2-family inhibitors IS20 and IS21
summary: Machine-learning-guided virtual screening followed by surface-plasmon-resonance and biological assays identified IS20 and IS21 as compounds binding anti-apoptotic Bcl-2, Bcl-xL and Mcl-1 proteins. Both affected cancer-cell viability and induced apoptosis/autophagic flux in tested cell models; IS21 also reduced tumor growth in leukemia and melanoma mouse models.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-guided virtual screening (model family not named in PubMed abstract)
organization: IRCCS Regina Elena National Cancer Institute; Sapienza University of Rome; Italian National Research Council and collaborators
tested: Machine-learning-guided virtual screening followed by surface-plasmon-resonance and biological assays identified IS20 and IS21 as compounds binding anti-apoptotic Bcl-2, Bcl-xL and Mcl-1 proteins.
unknown: The article calls the compounds potential/new leads; findings are biochemical, cell-based and mouse-model preclinical evidence. It does not establish clinical effectiveness. The PubMed abstract does not specify the machine-learning algorithm, so no specific model architecture is attributed here.
ai_role: Machine-learning-guided virtual screening prioritized putative Bcl-2-family inhibitor compounds; the candidate hits were then evaluated by surface plasmon resonance and in vitro cell assays, and IS21 was evaluated in mouse tumor models. The reported outcome is the specific assay characterization of IS20 and IS21.
source_review: null

title: Deep-learning virtual screening finds antibacterial hits in over one billion compounds
summary: Genentech and collaborators trained the deep-learning model GNEprop on high-throughput screening data and screened more than 1.4 billion synthetically accessible molecules. In follow-up experiments, 82 selected compounds showed antibacterial activity against the sensitized E. coli ΔtolC strain; the paper reports a 90-fold higher hit rate than the training screen and describes chemically diverse hits, some with activity beyond that strain and validated biological targets.
ai_technology: GNEprop deep-learning antibacterial activity predictor
organization: Genentech Research and Early Development; NVIDIA; Mila–Université de Montréal collaborators
tested: In follow-up experiments, 82 selected compounds showed antibacterial activity against the sensitized E. coli ΔtolC strain; the paper reports a 90-fold higher hit rate than the training screen and describes chemically diverse hits, some with activity beyond that strain and validated biological targets.
unknown: The 82 confirmed hits were tested for single-dose activity against the sensitized E. coli ΔtolC screening strain; this is not evidence that all 82 work against wild-type bacteria or in infections. The 90-fold improvement refers to hit rate relative to the HTS training experiment. Some additional compounds were selected for dose-response testing; do not imply all virtual hits were validated. A publisher correction fixed a coauthor’s misspelled first name and did not change results.
ai_role: GNEprop was trained on approximately two million small molecules screened against E. coli ΔtolC and used to rank a much larger synthetically accessible library for experimental prioritization. The follow-up assays confirmed antibacterial activity for 82 compounds; biological characterization also investigated specific targets.
source_review: null

title: Prospective machine-learning screen identifies six previously unreported OATP1B1 inhibitors
summary: Researchers trained and compared seven machine-learning classifiers for OATP1B1 transporter inhibition. In prospective CHO-cell testing, 15 of 19 compounds predicted active by SVC models inhibited the transporter; six (abamectin, asiaticoside, berbamine, doramectin, mobocertinib and umbralisib) were described as previously unreported OATP1B1 inhibitors.
ai_technology: Seven molecular-fingerprint machine-learning classifiers, with prospective selection by support vector classifier (SVC)
organization: Collaborations Pharmaceuticals; University of Arizona
tested: In prospective CHO-cell testing, 15 of 19 compounds predicted active by SVC models inhibited the transporter; six (abamectin, asiaticoside, berbamine, doramectin, mobocertinib and umbralisib) were described as previously unreported OATP1B1 inhibitors. The new candidate screen used contracted Eurofins assays; external execution is not a separate replication study.
unknown: The 84% refers to a small prospective test set of 19 compounds, and transporter inhibition was measured in vitro in engineered CHO cells. These findings flag possible drug–drug interaction liability; they do not show clinical interaction or patient outcome. The authors qualify six inhibitors as appearing novel at publication.
ai_role: Models trained on in-vitro OATP1B1 inhibition data ranked compounds for prospective testing. Researchers tested 19 model-selected compounds in transporter-expressing CHO cells and observed inhibition for 15, including six compounds the authors described as novel OATP1B1 inhibitors.
source_review: null

title: Machine-learning screening identifies natural RORγt inhibitors with preclinical psoriasis activity
summary: An ensemble machine-learning screen of natural products prioritized protoberberine alkaloids as candidate RORγt inhibitors. In vitro assays found that berberine and coptisine inhibited Th17 differentiation and directly bound RORγt by surface plasmon resonance; coptisine also showed efficacy in a preclinical mouse psoriasis model.
ai_technology: Ensemble machine-learning models for natural-product RORγt activity and counter-screening, combining graph neural networks and molecular-fingerprint random forests
organization: Bionsight; Incheon National University; Seoul National University; Kangwon National University; Ajou University; Wright State University
tested: In vitro assays found that berberine and coptisine inhibited Th17 differentiation and directly bound RORγt by surface plasmon resonance; coptisine also showed efficacy in a preclinical mouse psoriasis model.
unknown: Berberine and coptisine are known natural products; the novelty is their prioritization and experimental characterization as RORγt inhibitors in this workflow, not discovery of new chemical entities. The mouse result is preclinical and does not establish psoriasis treatment in humans. The catalog already contains an unrelated RORγt result involving topotecan; this paper's compounds and evidence are distinct.
ai_role: Ensemble models screened a natural-product library and prioritized predicted RORγt inhibitors. Chemotaxonomic analysis narrowed candidates to protoberberines; six were experimentally evaluated, and berberine/coptisine showed in-vitro effects and direct target binding, with coptisine tested in a mouse psoriasis model.
source_review: null

title: Machine learning reveals broad and previously uncharacterized fungal polyketide-synthase activity
summary: A genome-mining and cell-free enzyme study characterized fungal type III polyketide synthases (T3PKSs), revealing broad and varied substrate/product profiles. An ML model trained on 341 enzyme–substrate pairs predicted substrate specificity and guided tests that found two fungal enzymes, AcaePKS and PansPKS, active on all ten tested substrates, including non-natural substrates absent from training data.
ai_technology: Feedforward neural-network multilayer perceptron trained on protein-language-model embeddings and substrate fingerprints
organization: University of Groningen; University of Vienna
tested: An ML model trained on 341 enzyme–substrate pairs predicted substrate specificity and guided tests that found two fungal enzymes, AcaePKS and PansPKS, active on all ten tested substrates, including non-natural substrates absent from training data.
unknown: The enzyme products were characterized in vitro; the study examines product scope and biocatalytic potential, not native ecological roles or medical efficacy. Two candidate proteins expressed poorly, and the model's transfer accuracy was lower on non-fungal enzyme classes. The reported five enzyme sample includes only three well-expressing candidates, of which two showed the broadest tested activity.
ai_role: The model learned fungal T3PKS enzyme–substrate activity from measured data, was tested on unseen substrates, and predicted candidate promiscuous fungal enzymes. Guided experiments confirmed broad substrate activity for AcaePKS and PansPKS, including substrate pairs outside training data; cell-free assays and LC–MS characterized enzyme products.
source_review: null

title: CACLENS predicts and validates a zearalenone-degrading enzyme
summary: The multitask deep-learning enzyme-screening framework CACLENS selected ten candidate enzymes for zearalenone (ZEN) degradation, which were expressed and tested. One candidate degraded more than 90% of both ZEN and its analogue α-zearalenol (α-ZOL) in the reported assay.
ai_technology: CACLENS (Cross-Attention & Contrastive Learning-enabled Enzyme Selection), a multimodal multitask deep-learning enzyme classifier
organization: Shanghai Institute of Nutrition and Health, Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
tested: The multitask deep-learning enzyme-screening framework CACLENS selected ten candidate enzymes for zearalenone (ZEN) degradation, which were expressed and tested.
unknown: This is an in-vitro enzyme degradation finding; it does not establish safety of degradation products, remediation performance at environmental scale, or food/feed safety. The abstract does not name the successful enzyme or its degradation-product identity.
ai_role: CACLENS combined reaction-type classification, EC-number prediction and reaction-feasibility estimates to screen candidate enzymes. The paper then expressed and assayed ten selected enzyme candidates against ZEN; one showed >90% degradation of ZEN and α-ZOL.
source_review: null

title: Active learning discovers eight experimental binders for the LRRK2 WDR domain
summary: A free-energy molecular-dynamics and machine-learning active-learning workflow optimized compounds against the understudied LRRK2 WDR domain. Of 35 analogs experimentally tested, eight showed measurable binding confirmed by surface plasmon resonance and, for fluorinated compounds, an orthogonal 19F-NMR assay; measured dissociation constants ranged from 18 to 230 μM.
ai_technology: Active-learning-guided relative-binding-free-energy (AL-RBFE) workflow using molecular-dynamics thermodynamic-integration calculations and an ML affinity-prediction model
organization: Carnegie Mellon University; University of Toronto Structural Genomics Consortium; University of British Columbia; University of Ottawa and collaborators
tested: Of 35 analogs experimentally tested, eight showed measurable binding confirmed by surface plasmon resonance and, for fluorinated compounds, an orthogonal 19F-NMR assay; measured dissociation constants ranged from 18 to 230 μM.
unknown: The experiments establish ligand binding, not functional inhibition or a therapeutic effect. Confirmed Kd values (18–230 μM) indicate modest affinity, and the work is an optimization round around two previously confirmed challenge hits rather than an initial target hit discovery. This is not evidence of Parkinson’s disease efficacy.
ai_role: An iterative ML model selected ligand analogs for expensive free-energy simulations, using resulting calculations to choose compounds for further rounds and experimental validation. Of 35 procured/tested compounds, eight were confirmed as binding to LRRK2 WDR by SPR, with 19F-NMR used for orthogonal confirmation of fluorinated molecules.
source_review: null

title: Biological activity-profile modeling identifies SARS-CoV-2 antiviral leads
summary: NCATS researchers used biological activity-based modeling (BABM) to infer antiviral activity from compounds’ profiles across multiple assays. Of 311 model-predicted SARS-CoV-2 candidates tested in a live-virus cell-culture assay, 99 were confirmed active (32% hit rate); follow-up assays implicated viral-entry inhibition and/or autophagy modulation among confirmed compounds.
ai_technology: Biological activity-based modeling (BABM) models trained on multi-assay compound-activity profiles
organization: National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences, NIH; Public Health Agency of Canada; Florida State University
tested: NCATS researchers used biological activity-based modeling (BABM) to infer antiviral activity from compounds’ profiles across multiple assays.
unknown: Evidence is from cell-culture live-virus and mechanistic assays, not clinical treatment. 99/311 were active in the primary assay; further potency/secondary confirmations were available for subsets. Most confirmed compounds were reported to inhibit entry and/or modulate autophagy; these data do not establish safe or effective human therapy.
ai_role: BABM used prior activity signatures across assay panels to predict compounds with potential SARS-CoV-2 activity, including compounds outside conventional similar-structure hit finding. Researchers tested 311 model-predicted compounds in live-virus assays and conducted secondary/mechanistic assays on confirmed actives.
source_review: null

title: MISPOP machine learning screening identifies the oncolytic peptide Dermaseptin-S9
summary: The MISPOP ensemble screened a natural peptide library of 1,033 sequences, prioritized 16 oncolytic-peptide candidates and selected five for synthesis and testing. Dermaseptin-S9 showed membrane disruption and immunogenic-cell-death readouts in vitro and over 92% tumor-growth inhibition in a B16F10 melanoma mouse model.
ai_technology: MISPOP mechanism-informed ensemble combining XGBoost, deep neural networks and transfer learning with physicochemical priors
organization: Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine; Sichuan University; Naval Medical University; Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences and Peking Union Medical College
tested: The MISPOP ensemble screened a natural peptide library of 1,033 sequences, prioritized 16 oncolytic-peptide candidates and selected five for synthesis and testing.
unknown: The active peptide is a natural sequence rather than a new AI-designed molecule. Findings are preclinical: three tumor cell lines and a B16F10 mouse melanoma model (n=5 per group shown in article figures); they do not establish human efficacy or absence of toxicity beyond the tested model/doses. Only five of 16 model-prioritized candidates were synthesized and evaluated.
ai_role: The machine-learning ensemble integrated three predictors and mechanism-related physicochemical features to prioritize candidate oncolytic peptides from a natural sequence library. Five shortlisted peptides were synthesized and evaluated; Dermaseptin-S9 was tested in cell-based membrane-disruption/ICD assays and a mouse melanoma model.
source_review: null

title: Machine-intelligence design yields selective synthetic COX-1 inhibitors from a marine natural-product template
summary: Using Marinopyrrole A as a template, an automated design workflow generated and synthesized new natural-product-inspired molecules; target-prediction software pointed to cyclooxygenases. In biochemical assays, synthetic mimetics 2 and 2a inhibited COX-1 at 0.10 and 0.16 μM, respectively, and compound 2a was crystallographically observed bound to COX-1. Human platelet assays also showed inhibition.
ai_technology: DOGS rule-based de novo molecule construction and CATS molecular-similarity ranking, coupled with SPiDER self-organizing-map machine-learning target prediction
organization: ETH Zurich; Thomas Jefferson University; University of Bari; University of Innsbruck; Goethe University Frankfurt; Friedrich Schiller University Jena
tested: In biochemical assays, synthetic mimetics 2 and 2a inhibited COX-1 at 0.10 and 0.16 μM, respectively, and compound 2a was crystallographically observed bound to COX-1.
unknown: The study tests a small number of designed molecules; automated structure generation was rule-based and similarity-driven rather than a trained generative neural model. The COX-1 effects were biochemical/platelet assays, not clinical effects; the platelet IC50s for 2, 2a, 2b were 9, 13 and 56 nM, but COX-2 inhibition occurred at higher concentrations and selectivity varies by assay. Do not call these approved drugs or imply therapeutic benefit.
ai_role: DOGS algorithmically generated natural-product-inspired structures and suggested synthetic routes; CATS ranked candidates by pharmacophore similarity. SPiDER's cascaded self-organizing-map models predicted molecular target families, including COX. Experimental target assays confirmed the previously unrecognized COX-1 activity of selected synthetic compounds, with crystallographic confirmation for compound 2a.
source_review: null

title: Pinal designs functional proteins from natural-language descriptions
summary: The 16-billion-parameter Pinal model generated protein candidates from plain-language function descriptions. In four reported design tasks—fluorescent protein, PET hydrolase, alcohol dehydrogenase and metabolic H-protein—the selected designs displayed the intended function in laboratory tests; the best H-protein raised product titre 1.7-fold relative to native E. coli H-protein in a reconstituted CO2-fixation pathway.
ai_technology: Pinal, a 16-billion-parameter protein foundation model with text-to-structure (T2struct) and text-conditioned sequence design (SaProt-T) components
organization: Westlake University; and collaborating institutions
tested: In four reported design tasks—fluorescent protein, PET hydrolase, alcohol dehydrogenase and metabolic H-protein—the selected designs displayed the intended function in laboratory tests; the best H-protein raised product titre 1.7-fold relative to native E. coli H-protein in a reconstituted CO2-fixation pathway.
unknown: This is a primary-paper proof of concept with selected designs, not a broad hit-rate or industrial-performance demonstration. Experimental denominators vary substantially by task; extended data reports one active PETase among 94 screened and a fluorescent design selected from 29. The H-protein titre comparison was in a reconstituted pathway, not an organism or commercial process. No independent replication or therapeutic result is claimed.
ai_role: Pinal maps natural-language function descriptions to candidate protein structures and sequences. The team filtered and ranked model outputs, selected candidates for synthesis, and tested intended functions. The paper reports lab-observed fluorescence, PET-hydrolysis/esterase activity, alcohol-dehydrogenase catalysis and H-protein activity; the latter improved titre in a reconstituted multi-enzyme pathway.
source_review: null

title: Sequence-conditioned CogMol designs SARS-CoV-2 spike and main-protease inhibitors
summary: IBM Research and academic collaborators used the CogMol deep generative foundation model to design compounds from target protein sequence information alone for SARS-CoV-2 spike receptor-binding domain and main protease. In vitro inhibition was reported for two of four synthesized candidates for each target; the most potent spike-RBD inhibitor also showed activity against multiple variants in live-virus neutralization assays.
ai_technology: CogMol, a sequence-conditioned deep generative foundation model using a molecular variational autoencoder and protein–ligand binding predictor
organization: IBM Research; Diamond Light Source; University of Oxford; Enamine Ltd.; associated research centers
tested: In vitro inhibition was reported for two of four synthesized candidates for each target; the most potent spike-RBD inhibitor also showed activity against multiple variants in live-virus neutralization assays.
unknown: The source describes a proof of concept with a small selected synthesis set from roughly 100 ranked designs. Only in-vitro target assays were performed; the leading RBD inhibitor was also tested in live-virus neutralization against variants. The paper says ADME attributes were not experimentally validated and further work is needed to confirm inhibitor binding mechanisms. These are preclinical leads, not medicines or demonstrated clinical benefit.
ai_role: The team sampled CogMol conditioned on each target's amino-acid sequence to generate candidate small molecules; candidates were filtered and ranked in silico, synthesized and assayed. The model generated compounds without target-specific fine-tuning or target-structure input at inference; assays found micromolar inhibition for 2/4 synthesized candidates for each target.
source_review: null

title: Prospective deep-learning screen identifies nanomolar IRAK1 inhibitor scaffolds
summary: Ro5's prospective HydraScreen structure-based deep-learning screen ranked compounds for IRAK1 and was evaluated against a 47,000-compound robotic high-throughput screen. The study reports that 23.8% of IRAK1 hits were in HydraScreen's top 1% and identifies three nanomolar scaffolds, two described in the abstract as novel IRAK1 candidates.
ai_technology: HydraScreen structure-based deep-learning virtual screening, with SpectraView knowledge-graph target evaluation
organization: Ro5 (AI Chemistry); and Strateos
tested: The study reports that 23.8% of IRAK1 hits were in HydraScreen's top 1% and identifies three nanomolar scaffolds, two described in the abstract as novel IRAK1 candidates. The new candidate experiments were conducted within the Ro5/Strateos discovery collaboration.
unknown: This is prospective early-stage hit identification, not drug development or disease efficacy. The assay validated kinase inhibition in vitro. Authors are affiliated with the companies that developed the tools. The abstract describes two scaffolds as novel candidates, while detailed similarity analysis indicates one of three nanomolar scaffolds had a similar known active; do not call all hits unprecedented.
ai_role: SpectraView selected IRAK1 as the study target; HydraScreen scored docked ligand-pose ensembles to rank compounds before prospective screening. Researchers compared rankings with automated high-throughput assay results from a 47,000-compound library and reported nanomolar IRAK1 hit scaffolds, two described as novel candidates.
source_review: null

title: Machine-learning prioritization and CRISPR knockout identify OsWOX13 as a rice heat-tolerance regulator
summary: Meta-transcriptomic comparison of heat-tolerant and susceptible rice genotypes yielded 409 meta-differentially expressed genes. Random-forest and XGBoost feature ranking with SHAP independently prioritized OsWOX13; CRISPR/Cas9 knockout lines showed lower survival under heat stress (~20% versus ~60% in wild type) and delayed flowering, with accompanying changes in ABA, oxidative-stress markers and stress/flowering-associated proteins.
ai_technology: Random forest and XGBoost models with SHAP feature attribution
organization: Hainan University; Guizhou University; National Institute of Agricultural Science, Rural Development Administration (Republic of Korea); Pusan National University; Kookmin University
tested: Meta-transcriptomic comparison of heat-tolerant and susceptible rice genotypes yielded 409 meta-differentially expressed genes.
unknown: The PubMed primary abstract supports gene prioritization and knockout evidence, but does not establish detailed direct molecular targets or field-level yield effects. Reported survival figures concern the study's heat-stress condition and experimental lines; this is not evidence of breeding performance or resilience in field environments. Mechanistic pathway interpretations remain limited to associated physiological/proteomic measurements.
ai_role: The models prioritized stress-associated genes from meta-transcriptomic differences; OsWOX13 was among the top-ranked genes in both models. The team tested its predicted positive role using CRISPR/Cas9 knockout, followed by heat-stress survival, flowering, physiology and proteomic assays.
source_review: null

title: Machine learning uncovers new small-molecule chloride transporters from DrugBank
summary: After high-throughput testing 1,894 compounds and confirming 59 chloride transporters, researchers trained and evaluated machine-learning classifiers, then prioritized DrugBank compounds for wet-lab tests. Five of ten selected drugs—bazedoxifene, centhaquine, brilliant green, tamoxifen and nevanimibe—were classified by the authors as active chloride transporters, with an estimated 50–60% hit rate under their assays.
ai_technology: Machine-learning binary classifiers and consensus QSAR models trained on experimentally measured chloride-transport activity
organization: Tulane University; Rowan University
tested: After high-throughput testing 1,894 compounds and confirming 59 chloride transporters, researchers trained and evaluated machine-learning classifiers, then prioritized DrugBank compounds for wet-lab tests.
unknown: The paper combines a large primary high-throughput screen with a later ML-led DrugBank virtual screen; do not attribute all 59 initial hits to ML. The five drug-repurposing hits were measured in artificial liposome assays, not cells, animals or patients. The paper discusses assay artifacts: quinacrine/brilliant green interfere with the fluorescent assay, HCl salts can affect electrode readings, and evidence for brilliant green was weaker than for the other confirmed compounds. Authors report 5/10 active among selected candidates (or 7/12 including two known active compounds), not a generalizable clinical hit rate.
ai_role: After initial experimental discovery data were collected, machine-learning models ranked DrugBank candidates for transport activity. Researchers synthesized no new candidates for the virtual screen; instead, they tested ten prioritized available compounds in liposome chloride-transport assays. Five were classed as active; results extend these compounds' known pharmacology with membrane chloride transport activity.
source_review: null

title: CHOOSER uses protein foundation models to discover functional Casλ homologs
summary: The CHOOSER framework fine-tuned ESM-2 protein-language-model representations for alignment-free CRISPR-Cas discovery and pre-crRNA self-processing predictions. It nominated 11 Casλ homologs, nearly doubling the known Casλ set. Wet-lab work on selected homologs confirmed pre-crRNA processing for five of six tested proteins; EphcCasλ also cleaved target DNA and showed trans-cleavage activity, with a TTR PAM reported.
ai_technology: CHOOSER, a protein foundation-model framework fine-tuning ESM-2 representations for Cas homolog identification and Cas12 pre-crRNA-processing classification
organization: Tongji University; Zhejiang Lab; Shanghai East Hospital; collaborating Chinese research institutions
tested: Wet-lab work on selected homologs confirmed pre-crRNA processing for five of six tested proteins; EphcCasλ also cleaved target DNA and showed trans-cleavage activity, with a TTR PAM reported.
unknown: This is a specific functional genomics result, not evidence of a ready-to-use diagnostic or gene-editing tool. Only selected candidates were purified and tested; the paper reports pre-crRNA activity in five of six tested Casλ proteins and DNA-cleavage validation for a subset. EphcCasλ activity and PAM characterization are in-vitro findings. The article has a publisher-listed author correction dated 2025-01-09; this record relies on the version-of-record text and retains limited scope.
ai_role: CHOOSER mined candidate proteins adjacent to CRISPR arrays using learned sequence representations rather than alignment-only detection and prioritized Cas12 homologs by predicted pre-crRNA processing. The study reported 11 Casλ homologs and experimentally tested selected predictions; purified EphcCasλ was validated for self-processing pre-crRNA, DNA cleavage and trans-cleavage.
source_review: null

title: Deep learning designs selective antimicrobial peptides against Cutibacterium acnes
summary: A deep-learning design pipeline combining sequence generation and classifiers, transfer learning, pretrained protein embeddings and C. acnes-specific training data produced 42 novel peptides for testing. Five showed high-potency, selective activity against C. acnes, with MICs of 2–4 µg/mL; additional in-vitro assays tested activity against other microbes, hemolysis and keratinocyte cytotoxicity.
ai_technology: Deep-learning peptide generators and activity/selectivity classifiers using transfer learning and pretrained protein embeddings
organization: Shanghai MetaNovas Biotech; Fuzhou University; Metanovas Biotech
tested: A deep-learning design pipeline combining sequence generation and classifiers, transfer learning, pretrained protein embeddings and C. acnes-specific training data produced 42 novel peptides for testing.
unknown: All evidence is in vitro, with no animal or human testing. The 42 synthesized candidates are a selected subset of model output, and the abstract's five high-potency peptides have measured C. acnes MICs; activity against other organisms and toxicity is based on separate in-vitro assays. Do not imply topical efficacy or clinical safety.
ai_role: The models generated peptide sequences, ranked antimicrobial/hemolytic properties and incorporated C. acnes-focused training data. The team synthesized and tested 42 selected designs; five had reported C. acnes MICs of 2–4 µg/mL.
source_review: null

title: AMPlify prioritizes bullfrog-genome antimicrobial peptides active against priority pathogens
summary: Researchers integrated the attentive deep-learning classifier AMPlify into a genome-mining pipeline for North American bullfrog sequences. Of 101 candidate mature peptides generated from genome-annotated precursors, AMPlify predicted 75 as antimicrobial; 11 candidates were synthesized and tested, with four showing activity against tested bacteria, including a multidrug-resistant carbapenemase-producing E. coli isolate.
ai_technology: AMPlify, an attentive deep-learning antimicrobial-peptide sequence classifier
organization: Canada's Michael Smith Genome Sciences Centre, BC Cancer; University of British Columbia; University of Victoria; British Columbia Centre for Disease Control; Vancouver General Hospital; University of Washington
tested: Of 101 candidate mature peptides generated from genome-annotated precursors, AMPlify predicted 75 as antimicrobial; 11 candidates were synthesized and tested, with four showing activity against tested bacteria, including a multidrug-resistant carbapenemase-producing E. coli isolate.
unknown: This is a small selected validation set: 11 of 75 model-predicted candidates were tested and four were active. Results are in vitro and do not establish therapeutic efficacy or safety. Candidate precursor identification also used homology/genome annotation; attribute AMPlify specifically to mature-peptide prioritization, not the whole discovery workflow.
ai_role: After bioinformatics identified candidate peptide precursors from the bullfrog genome, AMPlify scored 101 mature peptide sequences and nominated putative AMPs. The team selected 11 predicted peptides for synthesis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing; four showed activity against one or more of six tested bacterial strains, including the carbapenemase-producing E. coli clinical isolate.
source_review: null

title: LSTM-designed peptides show antibacterial activity and mixed efficacy in a mouse sepsis model
summary: A generative long short-term-memory recurrent neural network produced 198 candidate antimicrobial peptides; five were synthesized. PEP-38 and PEP-137 inhibited carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella isolates in vitro, and PEP-137 also inhibited Pseudomonas aeruginosa. In a small mouse K. pneumoniae sepsis experiment, PEP-137 yielded 50% survival, PEP-38 did not improve survival, and the in-vitro-inactive PEP-36 control unexpectedly yielded 66.7% survival.
ai_technology: Generative long short-term memory recurrent neural network trained on antimicrobial peptide sequences
organization: Stavropol State Medical University
tested: In a small mouse K. pneumoniae sepsis experiment, PEP-137 yielded 50% survival, PEP-38 did not improve survival, and the in-vitro-inactive PEP-36 control unexpectedly yielded 66.7% survival.
unknown: Only 5/198 AI-generated peptides were synthesized. The animal experiment used one administration, small groups (12 mice per group) and a simple model; PEP-36's unexpected survival effect despite no in-vitro antibacterial activity complicates interpretation. PEP-38 did not improve survival; no mechanism, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics or safety was established. These are exploratory preclinical results, not a treatment claim.
ai_role: The LSTM RNN generated 198 peptide sequences, which were further filtered in silico; five selected candidates were synthesized and assayed. Two showed in-vitro activity against carbapenem-resistant isolates, and two were advanced into a mouse sepsis study.
source_review: null

title: Machine-learning-guided screening discovers potent innate immune signaling modulators
summary: At the University of Chicago, an active-learning pipeline iteratively selected molecules from a 139,998-compound library for in-vitro assays of NF-κB and interferon regulatory factor (IRF) signaling. After screening about 2% of the library, the study reported compounds suppressing NF-κB up to 15-fold or elevating NF-κB and IRF up to 5-fold and 6-fold, respectively. Follow-up cytokine assays found PME-4007 increased IFN-β secretion about threefold when co-delivered with the STING agonist cGAMP.
ai_technology: Machine-learning active-learning pipeline with variational-autoencoder molecular representations, Gaussian-process regression and Bayesian optimization
organization: University of Chicago Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering; University of Chicago Cellular Screening Center
tested: At the University of Chicago, an active-learning pipeline iteratively selected molecules from a 139,998-compound library for in-vitro assays of NF-κB and interferon regulatory factor (IRF) signaling.
unknown: The work reports in-vitro pathway modulation and primary-cell cytokine assays, not vaccination, immunotherapy efficacy, animal outcomes or clinical benefit. Fold changes are study-specific relative to agonist-only controls. A subset of candidates was further characterized; four tested compounds were flagged as non-viable by the cytostasis/cytotoxicity confluency mask despite strong pathway effects.
ai_role: Models were iteratively trained on screening measurements and used Bayesian optimization to select subsequent compounds for in-vitro testing. This model-guided selection led to the reported NF-κB/IRF modulators; follow-up cytokine release assays tested a subset.

title: Neural-network-guided autonomous experiments reveal an unreported TosMIC reaction
summary: A reactivity-seeking neural network coupled to an autonomous reaction platform navigated unknown chemical mixtures using real-time analytical data. Among the reactions it identified, follow-up characterization revealed an unreported photochemical reaction and a new reactivity mode for p-toluenesulfonylmethyl isocyanide (TosMIC): six equivalents of TosMIC underwent a multistep single-substrate cascade yielding a trimeric product in 47% unoptimized yield and forming five C–C bonds.
ai_technology: Reactivity-seeking neural network and junction-tree neural network integrated with an autonomous robotic synthesis and analytics platform
organization: University of Glasgow School of Chemistry
tested: Among the reactions it identified, follow-up characterization revealed an unreported photochemical reaction and a new reactivity mode for p-toluenesulfonylmethyl isocyanide (TosMIC): six equivalents of TosMIC underwent a multistep single-substrate cascade yielding a trimeric product in 47% unoptimized yield and forming five C–C bonds.
unknown: The source describes several found reactions, some previously known; this entry is limited to the distinct unreported TosMIC reactivity result. The reported 47% yield was unoptimized. The platform identified candidate reactions, while follow-up analyses and manual chemical investigation established the product and mechanism; no broad claim of fully autonomous mechanistic proof is made.
ai_role: A convolutional neural network classified reaction signatures from online NMR/IR/analytical data and a junction-tree neural network encoded reagent structures to help prioritize new experiments. The closed-loop system surfaced reactions; chemists then manually investigated and characterized selected outcomes, including the TosMIC trimer-forming cascade.

title: Machine-learning-guided optimization finds low-loading conditions for platinum-catalyzed amide reduction
summary: A machine-learning-assisted reaction-optimization study found conditions for reducing N,N-dimethylacetamide to dimethylethylamine using the known platinum complex [Pt(DMS)₂Cl₂]. The selected condition used 0.01 mol% catalyst and reached complete conversion in two hours at 39 °C without solvent, with a reported turnover frequency of 5,002 h⁻¹. The chemical catalyst identity is not claimed as new.
ai_technology: Sunthetics machine-learning reaction-optimization platform
organization: Ghent University Center for Sustainable Chemistry; Sunthetics; University of Padua
tested: The selected condition used 0.01 mol% catalyst and reached complete conversion in two hours at 39 °C without solvent, with a reported turnover frequency of 5,002 h⁻¹.
unknown: This is a single-substrate reaction-condition optimization on N,N-dimethylacetamide. [Pt(DMS)₂Cl₂] is a known complex; the reported finding is the ML-assisted optimized condition and measured performance, not discovery of a new platinum compound. The best-performing condition is reported after human-guided interpretation as well as model recommendations. The paper does not establish transferability to other amides, industrial scale-up or general performance across catalyst classes.
ai_role: The ML platform recommended reaction conditions across iterative experiments, using observed reaction outcomes to refine proposed conditions and reduce the number of trials. The team combined those recommendations with chemist interpretation and tested the predicted conditions experimentally; the source reports the optimized platinum-catalyzed reduction as a study-specific result.

title: Machine-learning and expert co-screening identifies two new silver-catalyzed cycloadditions
summary: Researchers at the Zelinsky Institute used unsupervised machine learning to filter and cluster candidate atom-economic cycloaddition reactions generated from quantum-chemical data, then used a digital co-expert and chemist review to prioritize experiments. The team experimentally confirmed two previously undescribed silver-catalyzed cycloaddition reactions yielding new products within about one week.
ai_technology: Machine-learning candidate filtering and clustering combined with the digital co-expert reaction-prioritization workflow
organization: N. D. Zelinsky Institute of Organic Chemistry, Russian Academy of Sciences
tested: Researchers at the Zelinsky Institute used unsupervised machine learning to filter and cluster candidate atom-economic cycloaddition reactions generated from quantum-chemical data, then used a digital co-expert and chemist review to prioritize experiments.
unknown: Two reactions were confirmed from a heavily filtered set of computational candidates, with final selection and validation by chemists. The reported approximately 180-fold acceleration is a comparison for the expert-screening bottleneck, not a general chemical-discovery speedup. The abstract does not specify individual products or reaction yields; no such details are inferred here.
ai_role: Unsupervised ML filtered and clustered computationally generated reaction candidates to reduce the set for review; the digital co-expert helped prioritize candidates. Human chemists made the final selection and performed experimental validation. The source reports two newly confirmed cycloadditions; the system was a human-AI pipeline, not autonomous discovery.

title: Bayesian optimization finds mild solvent-free mechanochemical conditions for cyclopropanation and epoxidation
summary: A Bayesian-optimization-guided mechanochemical study identified conditions for the established Johnson–Corey–Chaykovsky reaction using KOH in place of hazardous NaH, under air-equilibrated conditions and with no solvent or liquid-assisted grinding agent. In the chalcone benchmark, one optimized condition reached cyclopropanation completion in five minutes; the study also demonstrated cyclopropanation and epoxidation across multiple substrates, including yields of 45–75% for four additional substrates.
ai_technology: Bayesian optimization implemented with BoTorch/PyTorch, including multi-objective optimization of product yield and process mass intensity
organization: University of Parma SynCat Lab; University of Parma IMPLab
tested: A Bayesian-optimization-guided mechanochemical study identified conditions for the established Johnson–Corey–Chaykovsky reaction using KOH in place of hazardous NaH, under air-equilibrated conditions and with no solvent or liquid-assisted grinding agent.
unknown: The Johnson–Corey–Chaykovsky transformation itself is established chemistry; the finding is a measured, safer and faster mechanochemical process window rather than discovery of a new reaction class. A 5-minute completion time and other yields apply to the tested substrates/conditions; some prior solvent-minimized conditions could not be reproduced. The scale and substrate scope remain those reported in the paper.
ai_role: The BO models selected among six reaction variables (base identity/loading, time, milling frequency, liquid-assisted grinding agent and loading) using experimental yields and process-mass-intensity outcomes. Researchers ran the experiments, performed synthetic substrate-scope tests and used time-resolved in-situ X-ray diffraction to study milling effects.

title: Deep-learning screening identifies covalent SARS-CoV-2 main-protease inhibitor scaffolds
summary: A two-stage deep-learning screen selected cysteine-directed compounds for testing against SARS-CoV-2 3CL protease. Of 32 top-ranked compounds experimentally assayed, 12 inhibited the enzyme; six had IC₅₀ values below 12 μM, with the strongest reported at 1.4 μM. Five of those six exhibited time-dependent inhibition consistent with covalent binding.
ai_technology: Deep-learning COVCL and NOVCL classifiers integrating a directed message-passing neural network and feed-forward network
organization: Peking University BNLMS; and Peking-Tsinghua Center for Life Sciences; Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences Research Unit of Drug Design Method
tested: A two-stage deep-learning screen selected cysteine-directed compounds for testing against SARS-CoV-2 3CL protease.
unknown: Evidence in the primary abstract is biochemical enzyme inhibition and inhibition-mechanism assays. It does not establish antiviral efficacy in cells/animals or clinical benefit. Potency values are for the reported enzyme assay; most tested compounds were inactive, and the six sub-12 μM hits are early leads.
ai_role: The COVCL model first prioritized cysteine-targeted covalent candidates, then NOVCL ranked those candidates for predicted 3CL-protease inhibition. Researchers tested 32 selected molecules in enzyme assays and performed follow-up tests of time-dependent inhibition for active hits.

title: AI and developmental profiling reveal conserved rules for microRNA strand selection
summary: Using a high-throughput qPCR assay, Arizona State University researchers measured microRNA 5p/3p strand use across six Caenorhabditis elegans developmental stages and selected tissues. A machine-learning model trained on experimentally measured strand usage identified compositional and structural sequence features associated with strand preference; the learned relationships predicted strand usage in other vertebrates, including humans, and the authors report that the rules are conserved but context-dependent.
ai_technology: Predictive machine-learning model using 77 biologically informed features, trained on high-throughput qPCR measurements from the HiTmiSS platform
organization: Arizona State University Biodesign Institute and School of Life Sciences; Arizona State University School of Computing and Augmented Intelligence
tested: Using a high-throughput qPCR assay, Arizona State University researchers measured microRNA 5p/3p strand use across six Caenorhabditis elegans developmental stages and selected tissues.
unknown: The dataset measured strand usage in C. elegans across six developmental stages and specific tissues; cross-species including human results are model predictions/validation against available strand-usage data, not direct tests of gene-regulatory outcomes in human cells. The result concerns strand-selection patterns and predictors, not disease causality or therapeutic efficacy.
ai_role: The model learned strand-preference relationships from the experimental strand-usage dataset, quantified feature contributions, and predicted preference across additional nematode microRNAs and vertebrate species. Experimental qPCR measurements established the C. elegans profiles; predictions across species extend the analysis but are not themselves experimental confirmation of function in each organism.
