title: Biochemical-constrained generative AI yields experimentally active antimicrobial peptides against E. coli
summary: A University of Hong Kong-led team used a conditional variational autoencoder constrained by biochemical properties and a random-forest activity classifier to generate and prioritize antimicrobial peptides. In vitro testing of 54 generated peptides found 18.5% with MIC ≤10 μg/mL and 38.9% with MIC ≤50 μg/mL against the study’s E. coli model; nine peptides were classified as both active and non-toxic in the reported assays.
ai_technology: CVAE-BIO: conditional variational autoencoder with biochemical constraints and a random-forest antimicrobial-activity classifier
organization: The University of Hong Kong; University of Hong Kong-Shenzhen Hospital; Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences
tested: In vitro testing of 54 generated peptides found 18.5% with MIC ≤10 μg/mL and 38.9% with MIC ≤50 μg/mL against the study’s E. coli model; nine peptides were classified as both active and non-toxic in the reported assays.
unknown: Validation is in vitro, primarily against E. coli ATCC 25922; it is not evidence of treatment efficacy in animals or humans. The reported nine active/non-toxic peptides are assay-defined candidate hits, not validated drugs. This paper generated a different peptide set and used different training/design and testing workflows from the earlier C. acnes deep-learning, bullfrog-genome AMPlify, and LSTM Klebsiella sepsis studies in this ledger; do not treat the general AMP topic as a duplicate.
ai_role: The CVAE generated peptide sequences subject to predefined biochemical constraints; the random forest ranked activity using 30 biochemical descriptors. Researchers synthesized/tested 54 generated peptides in vitro, measured MIC and hemolysis, and reported the active/non-toxic subset.

title: Machine learning prioritizes ruthenium complexes with increased MRSA antibacterial hit rates
summary: Researchers trained machine-learning models on 288 modularly synthesized ruthenium arene Schiff-base complexes and used them to prioritize 54 new compounds for antibacterial-activity testing. The model-selected set had a 53.7% hit rate against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, compared with 9.4% in the original library, an approximately 5.7-fold enrichment.
ai_technology: Machine-learning activity-prediction models trained on ruthenium arene Schiff-base complex structures and antibacterial assay data
organization: University of Bern Department of Chemistry, Biochemistry & Pharmaceutical Sciences; National University of Singapore Department of Chemistry
tested: Researchers trained machine-learning models on 288 modularly synthesized ruthenium arene Schiff-base complexes and used them to prioritize 54 new compounds for antibacterial-activity testing.
unknown: This is a study-specific in-vitro antibacterial hit-rate enrichment, not animal efficacy, clinical validation, or an approved antibiotic. The comparison is 54 model-selected compounds vs the 288-complex source library, not a randomized prospective comparison with all possible metal complexes.
ai_role: Models were trained using assay data from 288 modularly synthesized ruthenium complexes and used to predict activity for a new set of 54 compounds. Those prioritized compounds were then assessed for antibacterial activity; the paper reports higher MRSA hit-rate in the model-selected set than in the original library.

title: Machine learning discovers D-amino-acid mixtures that boost anti-biofilm antibiotic cocktails
summary: A machine-learning-guided high-throughput screen identified a five-component D-amino-acid mixture (“D-mix”) with about 78% anti-biofilm activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa at 100 μM. Combining D-mix with half the lowest effective gentamicin dose retained about 91% bacterial-growth inhibition and about 93% anti-biofilm efficacy in vitro. In a small mouse lung-infection model, gentamicin/D-mix treatment reduced measured P. aeruginosa burden by about 95% in blood and 91% in lung tissue at 72 hours.
ai_technology: High-throughput screening coupled to machine-learning regression and iterative global optimization of D-amino-acid mixture ratios
organization: University of Science and Technology Beijing Institute for Advanced Materials and Technology; National Materials Corrosion and Protection Data Center; Beijing University of Chemical Technology
tested: In a small mouse lung-infection model, gentamicin/D-mix treatment reduced measured P. aeruginosa burden by about 95% in blood and 91% in lung tissue at 72 hours.
unknown: The in-vivo experiment used a small mouse P. aeruginosa infection model, not human treatment; study-specific bacterial counts and efficacy are reported at 72 hours. The composition is a selected mixture of five D-amino acids, with authors noting the full synergism mechanism remains unclear. D-mix alone was not bactericidal under the reported in-vitro conditions; effects are combination- and assay-dependent.
ai_role: Experimental measurements of mixture biofilm effects were used to train and iteratively update ML regression models, which guided mixture selection over design rounds. The selected D-mix was then evaluated with different antibiotics in vitro; the lead gentamicin/D-mix combination was tested in a P. aeruginosa lung-infection mouse model.

title: Machine-learning-assisted screening yields an experimentally active FtsZ inhibitor candidate
summary: A fused machine-learning and virtual-screening workflow narrowed compounds from three libraries to five candidate FtsZ inhibitors for bioactivity evaluation. The compound T3995 inhibited Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 6538 and Bacillus subtilis ATCC 9732 in reported assays, with MIC values of 32 and 2 μg/mL, respectively. Morphology and FtsZ-polymerization assays supported FtsZ-related antibacterial activity.
ai_technology: ROC-guided machine-learning selection combined with virtual screening, clustering and binding-model analysis
organization: Jiangxi Provincial Key Laboratory of Drug Design and Evaluation, Jiangxi Science and Technology Normal University; Jiangxi University of Traditional Chinese Medicine Cancer Research Center
tested: The compound T3995 inhibited Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 6538 and Bacillus subtilis ATCC 9732 in reported assays, with MIC values of 32 and 2 μg/mL, respectively.
unknown: Evidence is early in-vitro antibacterial activity and indirect support for an FtsZ-related mechanism; the abstract does not report direct target-binding measurements or in-vivo efficacy. Hemolysis was reported as safe at or below 16 μg/mL, while the MIC against S. aureus was 32 μg/mL, so this does not establish a therapeutic safety margin. The paper’s 2025 issue date follows its 2024 online publication date; the source-publication date here is the documented first online publication (23 July 2024).
ai_role: ROC-guided ML filtered candidates from three libraries; virtual screening of acquired compounds followed, then clustering and binding-model analysis prioritized five hits. Researchers performed growth, time-kill, cell-morphology, FtsZ-polymerization and hemolysis assays, including testing T3995.

title: AI-guided HuJ3 mutation improves HIV-1 gp120 binding and neutralization in assays
summary: The IsAb2.0 workflow, combining AlphaFold-Multimer complex modeling with FlexddG mutation scoring, proposed five substitutions to improve the binding of humanized J3 nanobody HuJ3 to HIV-1 gp120. Of these, E44R experimentally improved binding (ELISA EC50 1.696 nM) and neutralization relative to HuJ3; the other proposed substitutions did not consistently improve binding, and T99R failed to express. The gain did not restore neutralization to the parental llama J3 level.
ai_technology: IsAb2.0 antibody-design protocol integrating AlphaFold-Multimer 2.3/3.0, SnugDock, alanine scanning and FlexddG
organization: University of Pittsburgh School of Pharmacy; University of Pittsburgh Center for Antibody Therapeutics; University of Pittsburgh Center for AIDS Research
tested: Of these, E44R experimentally improved binding (ELISA EC50 1.696 nM) and neutralization relative to HuJ3; the other proposed substitutions did not consistently improve binding, and T99R failed to express.
unknown: This is a single, previously known J3 nanobody humanization/optimization case, not de novo antibody discovery, animal efficacy or clinical evidence. Only one of five proposed mutants improved binding; several predictions failed and the authors note limitations in prediction accuracy and manual steps. E44R remained less potent than parental J3.
ai_role: The protocol modeled the HuJ3–gp120 complex, nominated interface hotspots and computationally ranked five single-residue mutations. Researchers synthesized/tested variants in binding and HIV-1 neutralization assays; the measured E44R improvement is the experimental outcome, while most predictions did not improve performance.

title: Generative machine learning nominates a chiral ligand validated in asymmetric C–H activation
summary: A transfer-learned chemical language model generated novel chiral amino-acid ligands for palladium-catalyzed asymmetric β-C(sp³)–H activation, while an ensemble of 30 fine-tuned deep-learning regressors predicted reaction enantioselectivity. From 490 generated ligand candidates, mechanistic and synthetic filters retained 73; the authors tested selected reactions prospectively without disclosing the model-predicted enantioselectivity to the experimentalists. One highlighted reaction using generated ligand L5 gave 94% ee, matching the model prediction of 94%.
ai_technology: Transfer-learned ULMFiT chemical language model (FnG) for ligand generation and a 30-model deep-learning ensemble (EnP) for enantioselectivity prediction
organization: Indian Institute of Technology Bombay; Scripps Research
tested: From 490 generated ligand candidates, mechanistic and synthetic filters retained 73; the authors tested selected reactions prospectively without disclosing the model-predicted enantioselectivity to the experimentalists. The coauthor collaboration tested newly generated candidates; blinding experimentalists to model predictions is distinct from independent follow-up replication.
unknown: The accepted manuscript reports proof-of-concept prospective chemistry rather than a broadly validated catalyst family: only a small, expert-selected subset was tested and the authors report that some generated ligands were infeasible or failed to form product. The highlighted result is a ligand for an established C–H activation reaction, not a new reaction class; it does not establish scale-up or utility beyond tested conditions. The selected reaction gave 94% ee, but the accessible text table names it L5 and summarizes substrate/coupling partner graphically rather than in searchable prose.
ai_role: FnG generated candidate chiral ligands from a model fine-tuned on known ligands, while EnP ranked reactions formed by pairing generated ligands with known substrates/coupling partners. The researchers selected a small set for blinded prospective wet-lab testing; the paper reports one highlighted new ligand/reaction at 94% ee, matching prediction.

title: Generative antibody language model yields a pseudovirus-neutralizing XBB spike binder
summary: Tencent AI Lab and collaborators developed PALM-H3, a pretrained antibody language model that generates heavy-chain CDRH3 sequences, and A2binder to rank antigen-antibody binding. For SARS-CoV-2 XBB, which the paper says was not present during training, the selected generated antibody (Artificial 1) bound spike and neutralized pseudovirus in vitro, with reported KD 0.13 nM and IC50 0.00301 μg/mL. The study also assayed generated antibodies against wild-type, Alpha and Delta; performance varied by antibody and variant.
ai_technology: PALM-H3 pretrained antibody generative language model and A2binder antigen-antibody affinity predictor
organization: Tencent AI Lab; Peking University Shenzhen Graduate School; Xijing Hospital of Digestive Diseases, Fourth Military Medical University
tested: For SARS-CoV-2 XBB, which the paper says was not present during training, the selected generated antibody (Artificial 1) bound spike and neutralized pseudovirus in vitro, with reported KD 0.13 nM and IC50 0.00301 μg/mL.
unknown: The functional evidence is in vitro, using SARS-CoV-2 pseudovirus rather than live-virus or clinical outcomes. The study tested selected antibody candidates; several generated candidates performed substantially worse, so the reported top result is not representative of all generated sequences. The stated novelty is experimental neutralization against the XBB variant by a generated antibody, not proof of a treatment or protection in people.
ai_role: PALM-H3 generated CDRH3 sequences conditioned on antigen specificity using a RoFormer-based antibody model; A2binder scored antibody-antigen pairs to select candidates for binding, surface-plasmon-resonance and pseudovirus neutralization tests. The paper reports it generated and selected an XBB spike-binding antibody despite XBB being absent from its training set.

title: PROBY screening uncovers target-selective fluorescent probes for tau, BCL-2 and TDP-43
summary: The PROBY deep-learning pipeline screened 26,416 target-validated molecules for useful optical properties, identified 11 candidates for testing and found target-responsive probes PE859 (tau), obatoclax (BCL-2) and B3 (TDP-43). The study reports selectivity assays, cell/tissue labeling and ex-vivo tumor imaging with obatoclax. AI-guided structural modification of PE859 yielded 859-2, which enabled in-vivo two-photon and cleared-brain imaging of tau pathology in P301S transgenic mice; its measured tau-aggregate dissociation constant was 54.8 nM.
ai_technology: PROBY two-stage message-passing neural network pipeline (PROBY-L1 fluorescence classification and PROBY-L2 photophysical-property prediction)
organization: Children’s Hospital of Chongqing Medical University; Stanford University School of Medicine; Harvard Medical School and Massachusetts General Hospital; Sichuan University; South-Central Minzu University
tested: The PROBY deep-learning pipeline screened 26,416 target-validated molecules for useful optical properties, identified 11 candidates for testing and found target-responsive probes PE859 (tau), obatoclax (BCL-2) and B3 (TDP-43).
unknown: The PROBY hits are repurposed molecules from a target-validated library, not newly synthesized compounds. Target/probe performance is assay-specific; tau in-vivo imaging was demonstrated in a small transgenic-mouse study (n=3), not humans. This entry describes probe function and imaging results, not treatment effects or diagnostic performance in patients.
ai_role: PROBY ranked target-validated compounds by predicted fluorescence and seven optical properties, enabling selection and experimental verification of target-specific probes; the team then used AI-predicted structural modification alongside synthesis and bioassays to optimize PE859 into 859-1/859-2.

title: CycleRFdiffusion-designed TP4 is a reproducible cyclic peptide binder to TREM2
summary: A structure-conditioned workflow combining CycleRFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN and HighFold generated and screened 1,500 cyclic peptide–TREM2 complexes and prioritized four candidates. The lead TP4 showed weak but reproducible TREM2 binding in spectral-shift, microscale-thermophoresis and surface-plasmon-resonance assays. The authors report favorable plasma stability and moderate metabolic stability, presenting the work as an initial proof of concept for TREM2-targeted cyclic binders.
ai_technology: CycleRFdiffusion backbone design, ProteinMPNN sequence design and HighFold structural prediction/screening
organization: Weill Cornell Medicine; Macao Polytechnic University; University of Gdańsk
tested: The lead TP4 showed weak but reproducible TREM2 binding in spectral-shift, microscale-thermophoresis and surface-plasmon-resonance assays.
unknown: The only reported lead, TP4, is described as a weak binder. The evidence is biophysical binding and stability profiling, not demonstrated modulation of TREM2 signaling, microglial function, disease pathology or therapeutic efficacy. Treat this as proof-of-concept binder discovery.
ai_role: The AI pipeline generated and ranked 1,500 candidate cyclic peptide–TREM2 complexes based on structure, sequence and predicted energetics, from which four were selected for experiments; TP4 was then assessed with multiple orthogonal binding assays.

title: AI-guided natural-product-inspired molecules inhibit two multidrug-resistance transporters
summary: Combining marine natural-product fragment mining, AI-based molecular generation and structure-guided selection, the authors designed optimized analogues Ib18 and It12 targeting the ABC transporters P-glycoprotein (ABCB1) and BCRP (ABCG2). Both analogues reversed transporter-mediated resistance in overexpressing cells and outperformed reference inhibitors. Target-engagement assays supported transporter inhibition without expression downregulation. In xenografts, Ib18 increased mitoxantrone antitumor activity and tumor accumulation without a detected increase in systemic toxicity.
ai_technology: AI-based molecular generation integrated with marine natural-product fragment mining and structure-guided prioritization
organization: Zhejiang University of Technology; Zhejiang–Egypt Joint Laboratory on Intelligent Discovery of Marine Drugs; Zhejiang Provincial People’s Hospital; University of Pittsburgh
tested: Target-engagement assays supported transporter inhibition without expression downregulation.
unknown: The evidence is cellular and preclinical xenograft evidence, not patient efficacy or established clinical safety. The abstract reports no systemic toxicity increase in the studied xenograft setting, which should not be generalized. It does not give quantitative potency values or detailed comparator identities in the abstract.
ai_role: AI-based generation contributed candidates to a natural-product-inspired library; structure-guided prioritization selected optimized analogues for synthesis and functional tests. The authors tested Ib18 and It12 in transporter-overexpressing cells and evaluated Ib18 with mitoxantrone in xenografts.

title: LIMITS-guided peptide design yields selective anti-tuberculosis host-defense peptides
summary: The Penn State/University of Minnesota team used the Lead Informed Machine Interrogation of Therapeutic Sequences (LIMITS) workflow to train random-forest and neural-network predictors on approximately 100 host-defense peptides, using lead mutational scans and biophysical sequence features. Experimentally tested neural-network-designed MAD5.1 and MAD5.3 showed reported MICs of 5 μM against M. tuberculosis H37Rv, selectivity indices >16 against an eight-organism non-mycobacterial panel, and mammalian-cell toxicity indices >100. The study identifies peptide length as a potentially underappreciated activity determinant.
ai_technology: LIMITS (Lead Informed Machine Interrogation of Therapeutic Sequences), using random-forest and feed-forward neural-network predictors
organization: Pennsylvania State University; University of Minnesota
tested: Experimentally tested neural-network-designed MAD5.1 and MAD5.3 showed reported MICs of 5 μM against M. tuberculosis H37Rv, selectivity indices >16 against an eight-organism non-mycobacterial panel, and mammalian-cell toxicity indices >100.
unknown: This is preclinical in-vitro peptide evidence, not animal efficacy or clinical treatment. The paper reports that MAD5.3 did not produce a statistically significant reduction in H37Rv viability after seven days of culture despite its MIC and selectivity/toxicity metrics; do not generalize the headline activity to every candidate or assay. MAD2.2 was moderately hemolytic. The 5 μM H37Rv MIC and high indices apply to selected peptides and stated assay conditions.
ai_role: Lead-candidate mutational scanning informed feature selection and training on a limited ~100-peptide dataset; the models iteratively selected candidate anti-TB peptide sequences for synthesis and bacteriological testing. NN-predicted MAD5 sequences were assayed against virulent and avirulent M. tuberculosis strains and counter-screened against other bacteria and mammalian cells.

title: AI generates compounds with experimentally validated pancreatic cancer cell selectivity
summary: The IRB Barcelona team trained cell-line cytotoxicity predictors on data from more than 11,000 compounds assayed across pancreatic-cancer and control cell lines, then integrated the models with a reinforcement-learning generative system to design molecules for cell-selective effects. In follow-up tests, 45 AI-designed molecules or close analogues were assayed; 20 showed the intended cell-specific cytotoxicity, and dose-response testing confirmed 18 of those 20. Across the seven selectivity exercises, at least one hit was found in five; measured IC50 values could be calculated for 12 confirmed hits and ranged from 0.97 to 16.6 μM in the targeted cell lines.
ai_technology: Cell-line-specific cytotoxicity prediction models coupled to a reinforcement-learning molecular generator (REINVENT-based workflow)
organization: Institute for Research in Biomedicine (IRB Barcelona), The Barcelona Institute of Science and Technology; ICREA
tested: The IRB Barcelona team trained cell-line cytotoxicity predictors on data from more than 11,000 compounds assayed across pancreatic-cancer and control cell lines, then integrated the models with a reinforcement-learning generative system to design molecules for cell-selective effects.
unknown: This is a proof-of-concept hit-discovery study using in-vitro cell-line assays, not evidence of tumor selectivity in patients or an animal efficacy result. Only binary cytotoxicity labels at 10 μM informed the predictors; 45 generated structures or close analogues were tested, with 20 showing desired phenotypes and 18 confirming in dose-response assays. Exact generated structures were not always the synthesized compounds, and measured IC50 spans 0.97–16.6 μM for 12 of the confirmed hits. The paper explicitly characterizes this as an early hit-discovery stage.
ai_role: The authors trained predictive models on phenotypic screening data from >11,000 compounds, then used their scores as rewards/objectives in a generative workflow to propose molecules intended to kill one pancreatic-cancer cell line while sparing another or control cells. Candidate molecules or close purchasable analogues were experimentally tested and dose-response validated.
source_review: null

title: Machine learning generates active daunomycin-binding synthetic nucleic-acid polymers outside selected sequence families
summary: The study combined in-vitro selection with a conditional variational autoencoder trained on selection data to generate high-affinity highly functionalized nucleic-acid polymer (HFNAP) sequences. Experimentally generated CVAE sequences bound daunomycin with reported dissociation constants of 9–26 nM despite having no apparent primary-sequence similarity to experimentally selected polymers; competition selections found selected generated variants performed as well as or better than sequences obtained after multiple rounds of high-stringency selection.
ai_technology: Conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) trained on in-vitro selection-derived HFNAP sequence/fitness data
organization: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard; Harvard University; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Brigham and Women's Hospital
tested: Experimentally generated CVAE sequences bound daunomycin with reported dissociation constants of 9–26 nM despite having no apparent primary-sequence similarity to experimentally selected polymers; competition selections found selected generated variants performed as well as or better than sequences obtained after multiple rounds of high-stringency selection.
unknown: The finding is target binding by synthetic HFNAPs, not therapeutic efficacy or cellular activity. Binding results are specific to daunomycin and reported assays; the authors describe sequences as having no apparent similarity rather than proving wholly unrelated functional mechanisms. Some competition performance was assessed by in-vitro selection rather than a clinical or organism-level test.
ai_role: The authors used the CVAE to condition generation of novel HFNAP sequences on predicted daunomycin-binding fitness, then synthesized/tested generated sequences in binding and competition-selection assays. The machine-learning model generated the active sequences; wet-lab selection and competition assays established their binding activity.
source_review: null

title: Deep learning designs abiotic miniproteins that improve antisense-oligonucleotide nuclear delivery
summary: A generator–predictor–optimizer deep-learning workflow trained on quantitative delivery assays was used to design abiotic Mach miniproteins. Twelve selected predicted constructs were synthesized/tested; the strongest library construct improved phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer (PMO) delivery nearly 20-fold over unconjugated PMO in the standardized HeLa assay, while the authors describe the best designs as up to 50-fold more effective than prior polypeptide-based variants. PMO–Mach3/4 also produced dose-dependent reporter-protein restoration in skeletal muscle, diaphragm and heart in transgenic mice after a single intravenous dose.

title: CHANCE uses tumor genomes to prioritize non-cancer drugs with activity in patient-derived cancer cells
summary: CHANCE, a supervised machine-learning model integrating patient-specific coding and non-coding mutations with drug and protein-interaction information, screened 5,197 TCGA/ICGC tumors against 923 FDA-approved non-oncology drugs. title: AlphaCD maps experimentally measured catalytic properties across cytidine deaminases and supports a high-fidelity editor

summary: A random-forest model trained on longitudinal electronic health records from 161,584 people across two institutions identified records associated with high-specificity autoantibody testing for systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs). title: Deep learning detects elevated tissue-derived cfDNA across cancer and cirrhosis cohorts
summary: A study built a fragment-level methylation atlas from 521 noncancer tissue samples spanning 29 human tissue types and used it with cfSort, a supervised deep neural network, to estimate tissue composition in plasma cell-free DNA. summary: Researchers used regularized machine-learning models to select sparse plasma-protein signatures for 10-year incidence across 218 diseases in 41,931 UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project participants. title: Deep learning identifies externally replicated fast and slow cognitive-progressor groups in early Alzheimer dementia
summary: Deep learning clustered cognitive and functional trajectories in 283 people with early dementia probably due to Alzheimer disease into fast- and slow-progressing groups. The trajectory groups were externally validated and independently replicated in a 2,779-person dementia cohort. A classifier using cross-sectional data at diagnosis predicted progression group in external validation with AUC 0.70 ± 0.01.
ai_technology: Deep-learning clustering of longitudinal cognitive/functional trajectories, followed by machine-learning classification from cross-sectional diagnosis data
organization: Fraunhofer Institute for Algorithms and Scientific Computing (SCAI); University of Bonn; Massachusetts General Hospital and Harvard Medical School; Boehringer Ingelheim
tested: The trajectory groups were externally validated and independently replicated in a 2,779-person dementia cohort.
unknown: These are prognostic progression groups, not established biological disease subtypes or treatment-response predictors. The classifier had modest external discrimination (AUC 0.70 ± 0.01). Trial-size reduction and cost savings were estimated by emulating hypothetical enrichment and were not demonstrated in an actual clinical trial. The study does not show improved patient outcomes.
ai_role: Deep learning grouped patients using multivariate disease trajectories; the authors then trained a classifier to predict those progression subgroups from measurements available at diagnosis. The model-supported fast/slow progression groups were externally validated and independently replicated in a separate dementia cohort.

title: Deep-learning histopathology identifies tertiary lymphoid structure features linked to stage II colorectal cancer relapse
summary: SurvFinder analyzed 6,950 H&E slides from 1,604 stage II colorectal cancer patients across four cohorts and identified tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) as prognostic tissue features. Its multi-view model integrated TLS morphology and spatial location; explainable analysis highlighted TLS maturity and position near the tumor periphery as features associated with relapse-free survival and adjuvant-chemotherapy outcome patterns across the retrospective datasets.
ai_technology: SurvFinder, a multi-component deep-learning pipeline: WSINet for prognosis-associated tissue features, SegNet for TLS segmentation/subtyping, and MVNet for multi-view risk prediction
organization: Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center; Sun Yat-sen University; Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital; Johns Hopkins University; Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center
tested: SurvFinder analyzed 6,950 H&E slides from 1,604 stage II colorectal cancer patients across four cohorts and identified tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) as prognostic tissue features.
unknown: This was a retrospective analysis of patients enrolled in 2012–2018; results do not establish prospective clinical utility. Associations between predicted risk, TLS features and adjuvant-chemotherapy outcomes are observational and do not prove treatment benefit or that TLS features causally determine relapse. The authors identify absence of prospective validation and real-world deployment as limitations.
ai_role: Deep learning autonomously identified prognosis-associated tissue features in whole-slide images, segmented and subtyped TLSs, and integrated morphological and spatial features for risk prediction. Explainable-AI attribution identified TLS location near the tumor margin and TLS maturity state as important prognostic features.

title: Machine learning identifies new CYP2C9-inhibiting drugs and drug metabolites
summary: A structure-, dynamics- and physicochemical-feature machine-learning approach predicted CYP2C9 inhibition and experimentally identified four drugs—vatalanib, piriqualone, ticagrelor and cloperidone—as strong inhibitors, plus sertindole, asapiprant, duvelisib and dasatinib as moderate inhibitors in reported assays. Vatalanib had a reported CYP2C9 inhibition IC50 of 0.067 μM. Separate metabolism assays characterized CYP2C9-produced metabolites for abemaciclib, cloperidone, vatalanib and tarafenacin.
ai_technology: Machine-learning inhibitor predictors combining CYP2C9 structural/dynamics information with inhibitor physicochemical properties
organization: INSERM; CNRS and Université de Paris; Conservatoire National des Arts et Métiers; Université de Lorraine; Nantes Université
tested: A structure-, dynamics- and physicochemical-feature machine-learning approach predicted CYP2C9 inhibition and experimentally identified four drugs—vatalanib, piriqualone, ticagrelor and cloperidone—as strong inhibitors, plus sertindole, asapiprant, duvelisib and dasatinib as moderate inhibitors in reported assays.
unknown: Inhibition and metabolite findings are from the reported in vitro systems and do not by themselves establish clinically relevant drug–drug interactions, exposure changes, or patient harm. Reported inhibition strengths are assay-specific; clinical relevance depends on dose, exposure and context and requires pharmacokinetic/clinical assessment.
ai_role: The authors used machine-learning models to prioritize drug-like compounds for CYP2C9 inhibition testing. Follow-up in vitro assays identified the listed strong and moderate inhibitors; CYP2C9 metabolism assays separately characterized metabolites of four drugs.

title: Deep learning enables multi-site bone marrow adiposity genetics in UK Biobank
summary: Deep learning measured bone marrow fat fraction at four skeletal sites in UK Biobank MRI data; after quality control, 48,608 participants contributed to genome-wide analyses. In the white-participant meta-GWAS, the study reported 67, 147, 134 and 174 independent significant variants for femoral head, total hip, femoral diaphysis and spine, mapping to 54, 90, 43 and 100 genes, respectively. Analyses also identified site- and sex-specific genetic associations and added signals in multi-ancestry analyses.
ai_technology: Previously validated deep-learning models for MRI segmentation and bone marrow fat-fraction measurement
organization: University of Edinburgh; University of Lille; Heriot-Watt University; University of Southern Denmark; University of Dundee; University of Southern Denmark and collaborating UK Biobank institutions
tested: Deep learning measured bone marrow fat fraction at four skeletal sites in UK Biobank MRI data; after quality control, 48,608 participants contributed to genome-wide analyses.
unknown: The GWAS, transcriptome-wide and colocalization results are statistical associations and candidate gene mappings, not proof of causal mechanisms. Ancestry subgroup sizes differ, and results do not establish clinical utility or disease prevention. The deep-learning measurement method was established in an earlier study; this record concerns the distinct population-scale phenotype and genetic findings. A 2025 author correction fixed a misspelling of AKNA as ANKA; it did not alter the reported analysis or findings.
ai_role: The study applied deep-learning models to segment four skeletal regions and derive bone marrow fat-fraction phenotypes at UK Biobank scale. Those AI-derived measurements were the phenotypes used in the study's subsequent genetic association analyses; the paper's genetic findings are not themselves outputs of a generative model.
source_review: null

title: Deep learning maps previously unknown disease signals in ECGs across two health systems
summary: Researchers independently trained PheWASNet on ECG and electronic health-record data from Stanford Health Care and Cedars-Sinai to assess 1,243 disease phenotypes. In held-out patient splits at both centers, the study reported previously unrecognized ECG associations for disorders including respiratory failure, neutropenia and menstrual disorders (AUCs 0.86, 0.83 and 0.84 at Stanford, respectively). Cross-condition model-output analysis found that 35 of 37 strongly detectable non-cardiac phenotypes shared signals with only four other disease outputs, and simple ECG measurement models explained some findings.
ai_technology: PheWASNet, a multi-task deep-learning model based on a one-dimensional EfficientNet architecture
organization: Stanford University; Cedars-Sinai Medical Center; University of California, Los Angeles
tested: In held-out patient splits at both centers, the study reported previously unrecognized ECG associations for disorders including respiratory failure, neutropenia and menstrual disorders (AUCs 0.86, 0.83 and 0.84 at Stanford, respectively).
unknown: This retrospective EHR-linked study establishes model-detectable associations, not causal physiology, screening benefit or clinical utility. The disease labels are diagnostic codes associated with ECGs within 30 days; results may reflect comorbidity or care context. The authors caution that generalization to other health systems and populations is not assured. Some detectable signals were explained by simple conventional ECG measurements, and the paper does not claim that deep learning is required for every association.
ai_role: The researchers trained separate deep-learning models on raw 12-lead ECG waveforms linked to EHR diagnoses at two medical centers, then used held-out patient test sets to identify disease phenotypes whose signals were detectable from ECGs. Cross-phenotype prediction comparisons and simple-model analyses were used to characterize shared and interpretable signals.

title: Machine learning finds plasma protein signals up to 14 years before Parkinson diagnosis
summary: Using UK Biobank measurements of 2,937 plasma proteins, researchers found 446 dysregulated proteins in incident Parkinson cases and used machine learning to select a 23-protein panel for prediction. The panel achieved test AUCs of 0.78 in incident and 0.795 in prevalent cases; nine selected proteins were already dysregulated 10–14 years before diagnosis. In a separate Parkinson’s Progression Markers Initiative cohort, a 16-protein subset shared between platforms achieved validation AUC up to 0.76.
ai_technology: Support vector machine and other machine-learning models, with recursive feature elimination for panel selection
organization: Johnson & Johnson; UK Biobank; Parkinson’s Progression Markers Initiative collaborators
tested: Using UK Biobank measurements of 2,937 plasma proteins, researchers found 446 dysregulated proteins in incident Parkinson cases and used machine learning to select a 23-protein panel for prediction.
unknown: The result is a retrospective biomarker/prediction study, not a validated screening test or evidence that intervention based on the panel improves outcomes. The external PPMI analysis retrained and tested models in that cohort rather than evaluating a frozen UK Biobank model; validation AUCs varied by visit definition, and the reported maximum was 0.76. Protein associations and co-expression modules do not establish causal mechanisms. It is distinct from the earlier 2024 iRBD study in this ledger (DOI 10.1038/s41467-024-48961-3): separate cohorts and a different 23-protein/14-year result versus an eight-protein targeted panel and up-to-seven-year conversion finding; this record does not claim first discovery of presymptomatic plasma signals in Parkinson disease.
ai_role: Machine-learning classifiers were trained on UK Biobank plasma proteomic measurements to predict incident Parkinson disease; recursive feature elimination selected a 23-protein subset. The authors then tested the shared protein subset in the separate PPMI cohort using its own train/test split.
source_review: null

title: Machine learning and tear-fluid proteomics identify a six-protein ALS signature
summary: In discovery samples from 49 people with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and 54 controls, mass spectrometry detected 876 tear-fluid proteins, of which 106 differed in abundance. Biostatistical and machine-learning analyses produced a six-protein signature (CRYM, PFKL, CAPZA2, ALDH16A1, SERPINC1 and HP). In an independent cohort of 51 ALS cases and 52 controls, Western blots replicated significant group differences for SERPINC1 and HP; their combination had the best reported in-silico discrimination.
ai_technology: Machine-learning models applied to data-independent acquisition mass-spectrometry proteomics and biomarker-panel discrimination
organization: Technical University of Munich; Helmholtz Munich; Ludwig-Maximilians University of Munich; University of Melbourne; University Medical Center Göttingen; Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences; German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases
tested: In an independent cohort of 51 ALS cases and 52 controls, Western blots replicated significant group differences for SERPINC1 and HP; their combination had the best reported in-silico discrimination.
unknown: This is an exploratory biomarker study with modest discovery and validation cohorts, not a clinically validated diagnostic assay. The article reports that only SERPINC1 and HP differences replicated significantly across cohorts; the six-protein signature is a candidate and its best discriminatory performance was evaluated in silico. It does not establish ALS-specific causality or clinical utility.
ai_role: Machine learning contributed to identification of ALS-associated differential proteins and pathways and evaluated discrimination by the derived signature. The selected tear-fluid proteins were then assayed in an independent patient/control cohort by Western blot; only SERPINC1 and HP differences are explicitly reported as replicated across cohorts.

title: Machine learning identifies serum protein signatures for progression from asymptomatic atherosclerosis to ischemic stroke
summary: In a discovery cohort of 43 patients with asymptomatic large-artery atherosclerosis and a validation cohort of 39, investigators combined serum proteomics with machine learning to distinguish acute ischemic stroke from large-artery atherosclerosis. XGBoost selected a three-protein panel (RNASE4, HBA1 and ATF6B; reported AUC 0.917, specificity 80%) and a six-protein panel distinguishing patients from healthy controls (reported AUC 0.971, specificity 86%). ELISA assays confirmed higher GUCA2A and FLNA in patient groups.
ai_technology: XGBoost machine-learning models applied to serum proteomics; DeepPRM-Stellar targeted mass spectrometry supported peptide validation and panel optimization
organization: Huashan Hospital, Fudan University; Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University; Xiamen University; Xiang An Biomedicine Laboratory
tested: In a discovery cohort of 43 patients with asymptomatic large-artery atherosclerosis and a validation cohort of 39, investigators combined serum proteomics with machine learning to distinguish acute ischemic stroke from large-artery atherosclerosis.
unknown: The abstract reports 43 discovery and 39 validation participants, but does not establish prospective prediction or external clinical deployment. The signatures are candidate biomarkers, not a validated clinical test. Reported performance comes from this study and should not be interpreted as patient benefit or causal evidence. ELISA confirmation is reported for GUCA2A and FLNA, not every protein in the ML panels.
ai_role: The study reports that machine-learning techniques were used to identify circulating biomarkers of progression and that XGBoost selected the three- and six-protein signatures from targeted proteomic measurements. ELISA follow-up confirmed GUCA2A and FLNA group differences. The models are retrospective cohort analyses; the study did not prospectively predict future stroke events.
source_review: null

title: MP4 text-to-protein design yields ATP-active proteins, including one with a novel fold
summary: The transformer MP4 maps plain-language prompts to protein sequences. The study reports two experimentally validated de novo designs that were expressible and thermostable and showed ATP binding and hydrolysis in vitro. X-ray structures at 1.30 Å and 1.77 Å showed that one design adopts a fold not previously observed in the authors’ structural comparisons.
ai_technology: MP4, a transformer-based text-to-protein model
organization: 310 AI; University of California, Berkeley; McGill University; Arctoris
tested: The study reports two experimentally validated de novo designs that were expressible and thermostable and showed ATP binding and hydrolysis in vitro.
unknown: Only two designed proteins are described as experimentally validated in the abstract; this is an early proof of concept, not a demonstrated general success rate. ATP binding and hydrolysis are in-vitro results, not a novel physiological function or therapeutic effect. The source describes one fold as novel; no claim is made that both structures are novel.
ai_role: MP4 converted natural-language protein specifications into candidate sequences. Researchers evaluated 96 prompts in silico, selected candidates, expressed and tested designs, and solved two crystal structures. The source attributes the designed sequences to MP4; experimental teams established expression, thermostability, ATP binding/hydrolysis and structural novelty.

title: A graph neural network nominates OSM–OSMR for melanoma immunotherapy, with ex-vivo explant evidence
summary: MIDAS, a multimodal graph-neural-network model, ranked candidate immuno-oncology targets from gene-interaction, patient multi-omic and immune-biology data. In eight stage III/IV melanoma patient-derived explants, researchers blocked OSM–OSMR signalling with an anti-OSM antibody. The paper reports reduced dysfunctional CD8+ T-cell populations and lower CCL4 levels; PTPN22 inhibition did not produce comparable changes in this assay.
ai_technology: MIDAS, a multimodal graph neural network for immuno-oncology target ranking
organization: University College London; The Francis Crick Institute; Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust; University College London Hospitals; Royal Holloway, University of London
tested: The paper reports reduced dysfunctional CD8+ T-cell populations and lower CCL4 levels; PTPN22 inhibition did not produce comparable changes in this assay.
unknown: Functional follow-up used only eight stage III/IV melanoma patient-derived explants. This is an ex-vivo preclinical result, not treatment of patients or evidence of clinical benefit. OSM–OSMR biology has prior literature in other tumour settings; the new paper-specific contribution is MIDAS target nomination and measured perturbation effects in melanoma explants. Do not generalize to other cancers or claim a validated therapy.
ai_role: MIDAS integrated gene-interaction networks with patient multi-omics, immune-cell biology and genetic-perturbation evidence to rank candidate immunotherapy targets. Researchers selected OSM–OSMR for functional follow-up and tested pathway blockade in patient-derived tumour explants; the model nominated the target, while the ex-vivo experiments measured the T-cell and cytokine outcomes.

title: Machine-learning metabolomics identifies DHEAS and citrate signatures in anti-MDA5 dermatomyositis
summary: In a single-centre cohort of 183 patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathy and 104 healthy controls, seven machine-learning classifiers and LASSO feature selection were used with plasma and PBMC metabolomics to distinguish anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis. DHEAS and citrate were selected across the integrated analyses; plasma assays showed lower levels in anti-MDA5-positive cases, with concordant patterns reported in a separate 33-patient/33-control validation cohort. Within cases, DHEAS correlated inversely with rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease and citrate with rash.
ai_technology: Seven machine-learning classifiers (including random forest and XGBoost) with LASSO feature selection
organization: The First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University
tested: In a single-centre cohort of 183 patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathy and 104 healthy controls, seven machine-learning classifiers and LASSO feature selection were used with plasma and PBMC metabolomics to distinguish anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis.
unknown: Single-centre study with a relatively small validation group (33 anti-MDA5-positive cases and 33 controls). The metabolite associations with RP-ILD and rash are observational and do not establish causality. Reported discrimination is exploratory and does not establish a clinical diagnostic test or patient benefit; no treatment response was studied. DHEAS and citrate are known metabolites; the paper-specific result is their measured profile and candidate biomarker association in this disease cohort.
ai_role: The models ranked discriminatory metabolites and selected features for disease classification; the team integrated these with pathway results to prioritize candidate biomarkers. DHEAS and citrate were then measured using ELISA and a biochemical assay, with patterns assessed in the validation cohort. Machine learning aided biomarker selection and classification; assays and clinical data supplied validation.

title: Machine-learning metabolomics prioritizes succinate in sepsis-associated encephalopathy
summary: In plasma samples from 29 controls, 32 sepsis patients and 27 patients with sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE), LC–MS/MS plus machine-learning feature selection identified a 12-metabolite profile. Succinate rose stepwise from controls to sepsis to SAE, ranked among the five leading XGBoost features, and correlated with APACHE II, SOFA and lactate. In a cecal-ligation-and-puncture mouse model, dietary succinate supplementation before sepsis worsened cognitive-test performance, neuronal injury and microglial activation; succinate also increased inflammatory gene expression in cultured microglia.
ai_technology: Random forest and support-vector-machine feature ranking with XGBoost classification
organization: Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology
tested: In a cecal-ligation-and-puncture mouse model, dietary succinate supplementation before sepsis worsened cognitive-test performance, neuronal injury and microglial activation; succinate also increased inflammatory gene expression in cultured microglia.
unknown: The human discovery cohort comprised 88 participants and the held-out model test set had 18 participants, so diagnostic performance and metabolite ranking need larger external cohorts. Succinate supplementation was given before CLP in mice, and cell experiments used a microglial cell line; these are preclinical perturbations and do not prove that succinate causes human SAE or that targeting it improves patient outcomes. Associations with severity scores are observational.
ai_role: Machine-learning feature selection and classifier comparison were applied to the measured plasma metabolomics to identify discriminatory features; succinate ranked among the top five XGBoost features. Researchers then tested its functional relevance through supplementation in a mouse sepsis model and in cultured microglia. The animal/cell experiments were human-directed follow-up, not model-generated predictions.

title: Machine learning and Mendelian randomization prioritize CA2 as a diabetic nephropathy biomarker
summary: Across six kidney-expression datasets, researchers identified 314 differentially expressed genes in diabetic nephropathy and used LASSO, SVM-RFE and random forest to prioritize seven candidate genes. Mendelian-randomization integration further prioritized carbonic anhydrase II (CA2); its ROC AUC exceeded 0.878 across the analyzed datasets. The authors also reported qPCR validation of CA2 in clinical patient and control samples and an association with inferred immune-cell infiltration.
ai_technology: LASSO, support-vector-machine recursive feature elimination and random-forest feature selection
organization: Shanghai Tenth People’s Hospital, Tongji University School of Medicine; Yangpu Hospital, Tongji University School of Medicine
tested: The authors also reported qPCR validation of CA2 in clinical patient and control samples and an association with inferred immune-cell infiltration.
unknown: This is a candidate biomarker study, not evidence of a clinically deployed test or patient benefit. Reported AUC values are retrospective dataset performance; qPCR validation supports differential expression but does not establish CA2 as causal or disease-specific. The accessible abstract does not report the clinical validation sample size, so none is inferred.
ai_role: Three machine-learning approaches integrated candidate-gene selection from kidney-expression datasets; Mendelian randomization with expression-QTL data then prioritized CA2, which was evaluated as a diagnostic biomarker and measured by qPCR in clinical samples. The models supported gene prioritization and discrimination, while qPCR supplied the wet-lab follow-up.

title: Machine learning prioritizes 1-methylnicotinamide as a serum signal across HBV cirrhosis-to-HCC progression
summary: Untargeted serum metabolomics from 69 participants, including eight patients followed from HBV-related cirrhosis to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), was analyzed with LASSO and random forest to prioritize metabolites. 1-methylnicotinamide (1-MNAM) declined across healthy, cirrhosis and HCC groups and was lower at the HCC than cirrhosis stage in the eight progressors. Targeted mass spectrometry in a separate cohort of 25 healthy controls and 25 early-stage HCC patients confirmed lower 1-MNAM in HCC (AUC 0.954 for HCC versus healthy controls).
ai_technology: LASSO regression and random forest classifier applied to serum metabolomics
organization: Centre for Medical Research, Ningbo No. 2 Hospital; Liver Disease Department of Integrative Medicine, Ningbo No. 2 Hospital
tested: Targeted mass spectrometry in a separate cohort of 25 healthy controls and 25 early-stage HCC patients confirmed lower 1-MNAM in HCC (AUC 0.954 for HCC versus healthy controls).
unknown: The longitudinal transition signal comes from eight HBV-cirrhosis patients who progressed during follow-up. The independent targeted cohort compared 25 early-HCC patients with 25 healthy controls; it did not validate prediction of progression among cirrhosis patients. The authors describe the overall sample as small and call for larger prospective validation. 1-MNAM is a known endogenous metabolite; this record concerns the study-specific association and selection result, not discovery of a new compound, causal mechanism, or clinical test.
ai_role: The authors used LASSO and random forest to select ten candidate metabolites distinguishing cirrhosis from HCC, then identified 1-MNAM as the sole candidate with a consistent decline across healthy, cirrhosis and HCC groups. The algorithms prioritized the measured metabolite; targeted mass spectrometry in a separate cohort provided assay follow-up.

title: Multi-omics machine learning identifies lysophosphatidic acid in PRRSV infection and links it to immune suppression
summary: Machine-learning analysis of untargeted serum metabolomic and lipidomic profiles from clinical pig cohorts identified lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) as a PRRSV-associated biomarker. Follow-up infection experiments reported increased LPA with autotaxin upregulation; in porcine alveolar macrophages, LPA manipulation altered RIG-I/type-I-interferon responses and viral replication. In infected pigs, targeting LPA was reported to protect against infection and associated disease outcomes.
ai_technology: Random-forest analysis of serum metabolomic and lipidomic profiles
organization: Sun Yat-sen University; Huazhong Agricultural University; Wen’s Foodstuff Group Co. Ltd.; Stanford University
tested: Machine-learning analysis of untargeted serum metabolomic and lipidomic profiles from clinical pig cohorts identified lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) as a PRRSV-associated biomarker.
unknown: The clinical classifier and biomarker work concerns pigs, not human diagnosis. The infection challenge experiments were small (figure descriptions report five piglets per group), and cell assays were performed in vitro. The authors report that the mechanism by which LPA suppresses RIG-I remains unclear; the findings do not establish a treatment for people or broad field effectiveness in livestock.
ai_role: Random-forest analysis ranked metabolite and lipid features from clinical PRRSV-positive and negative pig cohorts and contributed to identification of LPA as the candidate biomarker. The authors then tested LPA in infection models, including cultured porcine alveolar macrophages and infected pigs, to examine host-response and disease outcomes.

title: Machine-learning metabolomics distinguishes SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and RSV from respiratory swabs
summary: Untargeted metabolomics and machine learning identified upper-respiratory-swab signatures for SARS-CoV-2 positivity, followed by targeted LC-MS/MS profiling. Across 1,226 samples (521 SARS-CoV-2-positive, 97 influenza A, 96 RSV, 211 other respiratory viruses and 301 virus-negative), the best SARS-CoV-2 LightGBM model had AUC 0.99, sensitivity 0.96 and specificity 0.95. Separate models reported AUC 0.97 for influenza A and 0.99 for RSV. The top-ranked SARS-CoV-2 features included 3-oxo-heneicosanoic acid and 2-(4-hydroxyphenyl) ethanol.
ai_technology: Light Gradient Boosting Machine and other machine-learning classifiers applied to mass-spectrometry metabolomics
organization: British Columbia Centre for Disease Control Public Health Laboratory; University of British Columbia; Stanford University School of Medicine; Stanford Health Care; Chan Zuckerberg Biohub
tested: Separate models reported AUC 0.97 for influenza A and 0.99 for RSV.
unknown: This is an assay-validation study using stored respiratory specimens, not a prospective clinical-impact trial. Results establish classification in the studied cohorts and do not show improved patient outcomes or routine deployment. The source notes unresolved oxo-position/isomer assignment for several features. The metabolite signals are candidate host-response markers, not proof of virus-specific causal biology.
ai_role: Machine-learning feature ranking identified metabolite signatures in untargeted profiles; the team adapted candidate signatures to targeted LC-MS/MS, and evaluated classification in respiratory-virus sample cohorts. The models supplied the sample-level classification and feature ranking, while mass spectrometry measured the metabolites.

title: Multi-omics machine learning prioritizes a plasma lipid signature for active tuberculosis differentiation
summary: Machine-learning integration of plasma functional-omics data in two discovery cohorts and a validation cohort identified biosignatures that distinguished active tuberculosis from nontuberculous mycobacterial infection, latent TB infection and other lung diseases. Cohorts included 76 people in the TB–NTM discovery set, 72 in the TB–LTBI–other-lung-disease set, and 68 TB plus 30 LTBI participants in the validation set. PC(14:0_22:6) was the most important predictor and was lower in active TB; additional external datasets yielded reported AUCs of 0.77–1.00.
ai_technology: Multi-omics integration and machine-learning predictive models for feature selection and classification
organization: Inje University College of Medicine; Ton Duc Thang University; Hanoi University of Pharmacy; University of Copenhagen; Korea University Guro Hospital
tested: Machine-learning integration of plasma functional-omics data in two discovery cohorts and a validation cohort identified biosignatures that distinguished active tuberculosis from nontuberculous mycobacterial infection, latent TB infection and other lung diseases.
unknown: The article calls PC(14:0_22:6) a candidate differential-diagnostic biomarker. Reported AUCs vary by comparator group and dataset; they do not establish prospective performance, clinical utility, or replacement of microbiological diagnosis. The PubMed abstract does not provide all cohort-level assay details, so this summary remains bounded to abstract-reported information.
ai_role: The authors used machine-learning predictive modeling across integrated functional-omics measurements to identify and prioritize plasma signatures that discriminate active TB from clinically relevant non-TB groups. PC(14:0_22:6) emerged as the leading lipid feature; the analysis was evaluated across discovery, validation and two external datasets.

title: TriSCOPE links cell-type-specific Alzheimer’s expression programs to inherited risk loci
summary: TriSCOPE combined cell-level predictive modeling, donor-aware differential expression and pseudotime analysis across six single-nucleus RNA-sequencing datasets (about 4.2 million nuclei from 627 donors). It identified cell-type-specific predictively expressed genes that were often missed by univariate differential-expression analysis; conditional GWAS–eQTL colocalization supported 27 gene–cell-type pairs at Alzheimer’s risk loci, including pairs without significant differential expression. Selected gene signals and analytical branches were compared across independent cohorts.
ai_technology: TriSCOPE, using LightGBM-based multivariate predictive modeling integrated with differential expression and pseudotime analysis
organization: Harvard Medical School; Harvard College; New York Genome Center; Rush Alzheimer’s Disease Center, Rush University
tested: Selected gene signals and analytical branches were compared across independent cohorts.
unknown: This is a computational reanalysis of previously published, post-mortem cross-sectional datasets; it did not collect new tissue or perform perturbation experiments. The authors state the framework is for feature discovery rather than clinical prognosis, cannot establish temporal ordering, and requires functional perturbation studies to distinguish pathogenic drivers from protective or reactive signals. The reported cell-level AUCs are modest and should not be presented as patient-level diagnostic performance.
ai_role: The supervised machine-learning branch prioritized gene-expression features that predicted clinical Alzheimer’s diagnosis within cell types, conditional on demographics and APOE genotype. The study integrated those model-ranked features with donor-aware differential expression, pseudotime and GWAS–eQTL colocalization to nominate genetically supported cell-type programs.

title: Spatial glycan imaging and machine learning identify a serum N-glycan panel for HCC in cirrhosis
summary: Spatial N-glycan imaging of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tissue and paired serum identified thirteen altered glycan structures; glycoproteomics linked them to more than 50 proteins, and sixteen glycoproteins were assessed in a separate patient set. Machine-learning algorithms combining glycan/glycoprotein features with clinical variables differentiated early-stage HCC from cirrhosis in a case-control cohort of 100 HCC and 101 cirrhosis-only patients, with reported AUROC values across the algorithms of 0.88–0.97.
ai_technology: Machine-learning algorithms using serum N-glycan and glycoprotein features, age, sex and AFP
organization: Medical University of South Carolina; GlycoPath, Inc.; HTX Technologies; University of California San Diego; University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center
tested: Machine-learning algorithms combining glycan/glycoprotein features with clinical variables differentiated early-stage HCC from cirrhosis in a case-control cohort of 100 HCC and 101 cirrhosis-only patients, with reported AUROC values across the algorithms of 0.88–0.97.
unknown: The discovery samples included 53 HCC tissues and 23 matched sera; the 201-patient testing set was a case-control cohort, not prospective surveillance. The paper notes that sialic acid was removed before analysis, excluding an important class of glycan modification. It does not establish screening benefit or prospective clinical utility. Individual glycoforms were weak classifiers; performance came from combined feature algorithms.
ai_role: Researchers used spatial glycan imaging and glycoproteomics to select altered tissue and matched-serum features, then used machine-learning algorithms to combine selected glycan/glycoprotein measurements with clinical variables for HCC-versus-cirrhosis classification. The source reports model performance in an independent case-control patient set.

title: Multimodal AI distinguishes ten dementia etiologies across nine clinical datasets
summary: A multimodal AI model analyzed demographics, personal and family history, medications, cognitive and functional testing, and neuroimaging across nine datasets totaling 51,269 participants. It assigned probabilities to ten primary or contributing dementia etiologies and addressed mixed cases. The paper reports microaveraged AUROC 0.96 for dementia-etiology differentiation; model probabilities aligned with etiology-specific biomarkers and postmortem pathology. In a review of 100 cases, AI-augmented neurologist assessment outperformed neurologist-only ratings.
ai_technology: Multimodal machine-learning model combining clinical, neuropsychological, functional and neuroimaging data
organization: Boston University; Stanford University; Peking Union Medical College Hospital; Columbia University Irving Medical Center; University of Nebraska Medical Center; additional clinical and research centers contributing cohorts
tested: A multimodal AI model analyzed demographics, personal and family history, medications, cognitive and functional testing, and neuroimaging across nine datasets totaling 51,269 participants.
unknown: The nine-dataset analysis is retrospective and includes in-house as well as external cohorts. The 100-case clinician comparison is small, and the study did not test prospective changes in care or patient outcomes. The authors call for prospective studies before claiming improved patient care. Model probabilities aligned with available biomarkers and postmortem evidence but are not histopathologic confirmation for every individual prediction.
ai_role: The model integrated routinely collected clinical variables and multimodal neuroimaging to estimate cognitive status and probabilities for ten dementia etiologies, including mixed etiologies and cases with incomplete features. It was evaluated across independent cohorts and compared with neurologist assessments; its output is the etiology-specific classification and probability result.

title: Machine-learning metabolomics prioritizes serum metabolites for SLE diagnosis and activity assessment
summary: Targeted serum metabolomics compared 89 patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and 44 healthy participants, identifying 146 differential metabolites. The authors combined statistical screening with seven machine-learning models to prioritize eight diagnostic biomarker candidates (reported AUCs above 0.95). Two additional metabolites, N-methyl-L-glutamic acid and L-2-aminobutyric acid, were evaluated by ELISA in a 90-patient SLE validation cohort and associated with SLE Disease Activity Index scores.

title: Machine-learning multi-omics links gut metabolites to GPCR targets and tau changes in Alzheimer’s patient-derived neurons
summary: A machine-learning and multi-omics framework screened 1.09 million pairs across 408 human GPCRs and 335 gut microbial metabolites. It prioritized orphan receptor GPR84 and the metabolite triacanthine, which activated GPR84 in a cell assay. In Alzheimer’s patient-derived iPSC neurons, agmatine reduced C3AR and tau markers, while phenethylamine reduced phosphorylated and total tau in the reported experiments.

title: Machine-learning selection identifies a six-metabolite signature for one-year cardiovascular events after PCI in type 2 diabetes
summary: VSURF feature selection prioritized six serum metabolites—ADPR, 1-methylnicotinamide, D-ribose 5-phosphate, nicotinamide, L-tryptophan and phosphatidylcholine PC(36:2)—for one-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) after PCI in patients with type 2 diabetes. Random-forest and XGBoost models were tested in a nested case-control study and an independent prospective cohort of 301 patients; in the external cohort, reported AUCs were 0.92 and 0.94 for MACEs, respectively. The study also linked NAD+ biosynthesis perturbation to altered bioenergetics, inflammation and proliferation in high-glucose-cultured human aortic smooth-muscle cells.

title: Machine learning prioritizes a protective Arabidopsis leaf fungus that suppresses oomycete infection
summary: Four classifiers (random forest, support-vector machine, logistic regression and multilayer perceptron) used six years of natural Arabidopsis leaf-microbiome data to prioritize taxa associated with Albugo infection status. Follow-up plant assays found that selected health-associated microbes reduced infection; Cystofilobasidium macerans OTU126 gave the strongest individual protection, reducing Albugo infection by an average of 73%. In a 15-member synthetic leaf community, adding this fungus increased the reported infection reduction to 40.25%, compared with 19.36% for the community alone.

tested: Follow-up plant assays found that selected health-associated microbes reduced infection; Cystofilobasidium macerans OTU126 gave the strongest individual protection, reducing Albugo infection by an average of 73%.

title: Machine learning identifies bacterial strains and combinations that reduce pathogen colonization in Arabidopsis
summary: Random forest and elastic-net models analyzed 136 synthetic communities, each composed of five bacterial strains, and identified strain identity as the strongest predictor of protection against Pseudomonas syringae DC3000 in Arabidopsis. Independent test communities confirmed predictive performance, and follow-up plant assays showed that Acidovorax Leaf76, Rhizobium Leaf68 and Pseudomonas Leaf15 each reduced pathogen colonization by about two orders of magnitude versus axenic controls; a Rhizobium Leaf371–Arthrobacter Leaf337 combination also reduced colonization.

title: Machine-learning-guided PBMC proteomics identifies SLE diagnosis and activity biomarker panels
summary: A random-forest and OPLS-DA prioritization pipeline applied to peripheral-blood mononuclear-cell proteomics identified candidate protein combinations for distinguishing systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) from healthy and rheumatoid-arthritis controls and for separating active from inactive SLE. ELISA in a separate 80-person cohort supported a six-protein diagnosis panel (IFIT3, MX1, TOMM40, STAT1, STAT2 and OAS3; AUC 0.723 versus healthy controls and 0.815 versus rheumatoid arthritis) and a nine-protein activity panel (AUC 0.990). title: Integrated proteomics and metabolomics with LASSO nominate a four-analyte early IgA-nephropathy plasma panel
summary: A study of biopsy-confirmed IgA nephropathy (IgAN) integrated plasma proteomics and untargeted metabolomics and used LASSO logistic regression to select PRKAR2A, IL6ST, SOS1 and palmitoleic acid as candidate discriminators from healthy controls. The panel had AUC 0.994 in the training set and 0.977 in the test split; ELISA assays in a separate 9-case/10-control sample set yielded an AUC of 0.91. Proteomic and metabolomic analyses also indicated complement/immune activation and altered energy and amino-acid metabolism in the studied cases.

tested: A study of biopsy-confirmed IgA nephropathy (IgAN) integrated plasma proteomics and untargeted metabolomics and used LASSO logistic regression to select PRKAR2A, IL6ST, SOS1 and palmitoleic acid as candidate discriminators from healthy controls.

title: Machine-learning proteomics prioritizes four plasma markers associated with ankylosing-spondylitis activity
summary: A plasma-proteomics study of 48 active ankylosing-spondylitis (AS) patients, 21 stable-stage patients and 35 healthy controls combined random-forest and OPLS-DA scores to prioritize candidate markers. SAA1, FERMT3, ILK and TLN1 were elevated in active-stage AS and returned toward control levels in stable-stage patients; ELISA in a separate cohort (27 active, 28 stable, 24 controls) reproduced these patterns. A combined ELISA model distinguished active AS from healthy controls with AUC 0.932. FERMT3, ILK and TLN1 are integrin-pathway proteins.

unknown: This is an observational, cross-sectional plasma-biomarker study; it does not establish causal integrin-pathway activity, prognosis over time, treatment response, or clinical utility. The independent ELISA cohort had 79 participants and was drawn from the same clinical setting. The combined AUC 0.932 applies to active AS versus healthy controls; discrimination against other inflammatory diseases was not demonstrated. SAA1 has been previously reported as an AS-associated marker; the AI-supported novelty is the combined panel and the integrin-related proteins, not discovery of SAA1 itself.

title: Machine-learning-guided electrochemical screening isolates five new reaction products
summary: A machine-learning-guided, chemist-in-the-loop screen predicted electrochemical reactivity for 38,865 potential partners with 1,4-dicyanobenzene (DCB). Automated tests of 20 prioritized, previously untested partners yielded DCB conversion in 16; five produced an isolable major product judged of synthetic or mechanistic interest. The reported examples include a silyl-enol-ether coupling and electrochemical benzylic arylation of benzyltrimethylsilane with DCB, plus three mechanistically unexpected products.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-guided reaction-competency classifier using a DFT-informed molecular representation
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; collaborating institutions
tested: Automated tests of 20 prioritized, previously untested partners yielded DCB conversion in 16; five produced an isolable major product judged of synthetic or mechanistic interest.
unknown: This is an early reaction-discovery demonstration under one fixed DCB electrolysis system, not a general reaction predictor or optimized synthetic platform. Seven of the 16 DCB-converting selected reactions gave complex mixtures without an appreciable single isolated product; five yielded isolable major products, reported at low yields and without method optimization. DCB conversion alone does not establish a product identity, and the three mechanistically ambiguous outcomes require further study.
ai_role: The model screened a 38,865-member virtual set for reaction competency and, with chemist selection, prioritized 20 new partners for automated electrolysis. The experiments measured DCB conversion, then product analysis isolated and characterized five major products from the selected set.

title: Machine-learning-guided photoredox design experimentally enables three transformations
summary: A workflow combining a variational-autoencoder latent space of 11,069 literature photoredox reactions with random-forest catalyst/reagent recommendations was used to propose three transformations. Experiments synthesized a previously inaccessible substituted dihydroquinolinone 43 using fac-Ir(ppy)3, a related oxidative cross-coupling product 46 in 64% yield, and heterocycle product 49 in 74% yield. The paper presents these as experimentally validated transformations identified through model-assisted precedent retrieval and condition selection.
ai_technology: Variational autoencoder for reaction-space navigation and random-forest multilabel catalyst/reagent recommendation
organization: Wuhan University; HOURS Inc.; collaborating institutions
tested: Experiments synthesized a previously inaccessible substituted dihydroquinolinone 43 using fac-Ir(ppy)3, a related oxidative cross-coupling product 46 in 64% yield, and heterocycle product 49 in 74% yield.
unknown: The work is a human-guided photoredox design workflow, not autonomous synthesis. The three examples were selected by researchers and use a literature-trained model; the paper establishes feasibility for these tested transformations, not general transfer or broad yield improvement. Reported 64% and 74% yields apply only to the specific demonstrated products; further optimization and substrate-scope work are needed.

Chemists used the model-suggested conditions to test three transformations, including two modifications beyond the reported precedent and one previously undocumented photoredox synthesis, then measured isolated product yields.

title: Cross-tissue machine learning prioritizes a 13-gene rheumatoid-arthritis activity score
summary: A machine-learning feature-selection pipeline integrated public whole-blood (1,885 samples) and synovial-tissue (284 samples) transcriptomic datasets and selected a 13-gene rheumatoid-arthritis score. Across five independent transcriptomic datasets, the score tracked DAS28 disease activity, distinguished rheumatoid arthritis from osteoarthritis, separated polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis from healthy controls, and was associated with treatment effects. In an independent immunoblot cohort, two of six tested proteins, TNFAIP6/TSG-6 and HSP90AB1/HSP90, were confirmed.

organization: University of California, San Francisco; Oregon Health & Science University
tested: In an independent immunoblot cohort, two of six tested proteins, TNFAIP6/TSG-6 and HSP90AB1/HSP90, were confirmed.

The independent protein follow-up confirmed two of six proteins tested, not the entire 13-gene panel, and validation in larger prospective cohorts is needed. Treatment-effect association should not be interpreted as prospective prediction of individual response.
ai_role: The pipeline selected a compact 13-gene signature from public blood and synovial expression datasets; the study evaluated its association with disease activity and diagnostic distinctions across five independent transcriptomic datasets, then tested six selected proteins by immunoblot in a separate patient cohort.

title: Random-forest metabolite profiling reduces false-positive newborn screens for four inherited disorders
summary: A 121-analyte LC–MS/MS panel combined established markers, untargeted-metabolomics features and chromatographically resolved isobars with random-forest classification of California newborn-screen dried blood spots. In 883 archived infant samples, the study reports that the second-tier approach maintained 100% sensitivity while reducing false positives by 83% for glutaric acidemia type I, 84% for methylmalonic acidemia, 100% for ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency and 51% for very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency. Several long-chain acylcarnitine and hydroxy-acylcarnitine isobar features contributed to classification, although their chemical identities were unresolved.

organization: Stanford Health Care; Yale University; California Department of Public Health
tested: In 883 archived infant samples, the study reports that the second-tier approach maintained 100% sensitivity while reducing false positives by 83% for glutaric acidemia type I, 84% for methylmalonic acidemia, 100% for ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency and 51% for very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency.

The validation sample was not a fully independent external set, and archived-sample degradation and processing batch effects limited biomarker discovery; some discriminating isobar identities and biological significance remain unknown. The reported sensitivity and false-positive reductions are cohort-specific and do not establish improved health outcomes or routine clinical utility.

Feature-importance analysis showed that complex profiles, including unresolved long-chain acylcarnitine/hydroxy-acylcarnitine isobars, contributed to classification; the model's second-tier performance was assessed against known case status.

title: 3D-HiChAT predicts embryonic enhancer hubs validated by CRISPR interference
summary: A random-forest model integrating ATAC-seq, H3K27ac ChIP-seq and HiChIP data predicted enhancer effects across mouse trophoblast stem cells, embryonic stem cells and extraembryonic endoderm cells. CRISPRi tests supported a shared Enh14 hub regulating both Tfcp2l1 and Gli2 in embryonic stem cells, and an Enh4 hub linked to seven genes in extraembryonic endoderm; four of those seven showed expression reductions as predicted. Across 40 tested enhancer-promoter pairs, experiments yielded 12 true positives and 13 true negatives, with overall prediction accuracy 0.71.

tested: CRISPRi tests supported a shared Enh14 hub regulating both Tfcp2l1 and Gli2 in embryonic stem cells, and an Enh4 hub linked to seven genes in extraembryonic endoderm; four of those seven showed expression reductions as predicted.
