Only selected predictions were tested; the 40-pair validation had 12 true positives, 13 true negatives and an overall reported accuracy of 0.71, leaving discordant/uncertain pairs. The Enh14 and Enh4 results support specific cell-type-dependent regulatory hubs but do not establish the full genome-wide predicted map as experimentally validated or prove developmental phenotypes in vivo.

Researchers selected predictions for CRISPRi validation and measured target-gene expression by RT-qPCR; the paper reports specific validated multi-gene enhancer hubs and positive/negative prediction rates across 40 pairs.

title: CellOracle-guided zebrafish perturbations identify axial-mesoderm effects of noto and lhx1a loss
summary: The CellOracle machine-learning workflow used single-cell gene-regulatory networks to prioritize transcription factors for perturbation in zebrafish development. CRISPR/Cas9 tests confirmed a model-predicted, previously unreported increase in prechordal-plate differentiation after loss of noto, alongside the known loss of notochord. Model-prioritized lhx1a loss also inhibited axial-mesoderm differentiation: single-cell RNA-seq found expansion of early notochord cells and reductions in later notochord and prechordal-plate populations; orthogonal RNA assays supported reduced notochord/prechordal markers.

tested: CRISPR/Cas9 tests confirmed a model-predicted, previously unreported increase in prechordal-plate differentiation after loss of noto, alongside the known loss of notochord.

The CellOracle model depends on inferred networks and makes cell-state-shift predictions, not direct causal proof of all inferred edges. A later unreviewed 2024 preprint raises implementation and benchmarking concerns, particularly about its use of ATAC-seq for distal regulatory interactions and comparisons with other GRN tools; this record relies only on the specific perturbation predictions tested experimentally and does not adopt the paper's broader benchmarking claims.

Researchers used CRISPR/Cas9 crispants, single-cell RNA-seq and marker assays to test the predicted zebrafish cell-fate effects; the prechordal-plate increase after noto loss was reported as previously unrecognized.

title: AcRanker-guided discovery of AcrIIA20 and AcrIIA21 anti-CRISPR proteins
summary: AcRanker, an XGBoost ranking model using amino-acid sequence features, ranked proteins from prophage regions in self-targeting Streptococcus genomes. Experimental testing identified two previously unknown type II-A anti-CRISPRs: AcrIIA20 (ML1), which strongly inhibited Streptococcus iniae Cas9 and weakly inhibited S. pyogenes Cas9, and AcrIIA21 (ML8), which inhibited S. pyogenes, S. aureus and S. iniae Cas9 with lower potency.

title: AI-prioritized CRISPR screen identifies ALOX5 and OXTR as regulators of keratinocyte IL17RA in psoriasis
summary: A genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen in primary human epidermal keratinocytes, combined with VirtualCRISPR language-model prioritization, identified ALOX5 and OXTR as previously underappreciated cell-intrinsic regulators of surface IL17RA. Targeted knockout in keratinocytes from two adult donors reduced IL17RA and inflammatory cytokine secretion. Topical inhibition of ALOX5 or OXTR also reduced disease signs in an imiquimod mouse model of psoriasiform dermatitis.

tested: A genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen in primary human epidermal keratinocytes, combined with VirtualCRISPR language-model prioritization, identified ALOX5 and OXTR as previously underappreciated cell-intrinsic regulators of surface IL17RA.

The authors combined screen enrichment with the model’s lower prior probability for noncanonical hits to prioritize high-novelty regulators; targeted CRISPR knockout and pharmacologic mouse experiments tested the resulting biology.

title: CellOracle-guided pancreatic islet differentiation experiments reveal STAT1 and ZEB1 lineage roles
summary: A digital model built from 400,603 cells across 61 single-cell datasets used CellOracle gene-regulatory-network inference and in-silico transcription-factor perturbations to nominate regulators of stem-cell-derived human islet differentiation. CRISPRi experiments supported a previously unreported role for STAT1 in exocrine specification: transient STAT1 knockdown reduced exocrine markers, and JAK–STAT inhibition preserved beta-cell markers and improved glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. organization: Washington University School of Medicine; University of Miami
tested: CRISPRi experiments supported a previously unreported role for STAT1 in exocrine specification: transient STAT1 knockdown reduced exocrine markers, and JAK–STAT inhibition preserved beta-cell markers and improved glucose-stimulated insulin secretion.

title: BacterAI experimentally maps amino-acid growth requirements of two oral Streptococcus species
summary: BacterAI autonomously designed and ran growth experiments with robotic liquid handling to learn amino-acid requirements for the oral commensals Streptococcus gordonii and S. sanguinis. It learned separate growth rules for each organism and showed that the closely related species have different amino-acid auxotrophies. For S. gordonii, its neural-network growth predictions exceeded 90% accuracy after nine days and 3,024 experiments; the article also reports transfer-learning tests in larger media.

organization: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; University of Michigan
tested: BacterAI autonomously designed and ran growth experiments with robotic liquid handling to learn amino-acid requirements for the oral commensals Streptococcus gordonii and S. sanguinis.

Replicate growth assays showed high agreement, but inferred rules may not cover every environmental condition.

It enabled an unbiased experimental mapping of nutrient requirements from a blank slate for both species.

title: Prospective multicenter validation of TriVerity links a 29-mRNA host response to infection type and near-term severity
summary: In the prospective SEPSIS-SHIELD study, a machine-learning blood test using isothermal amplification of 29 host-response mRNAs was evaluated in adults presenting to 22 emergency departments with suspected infection or sepsis. Among 1,222 patients with valid results, its bacterial and viral scores distinguished clinically adjudicated infection status with AUROCs of 0.83 and 0.91, respectively, and the system also produced a separate score for risk of ICU-level care within seven days. The test’s high/very-high and low/very-low interpretation bands had 92–99% sensitivities and specificities for selected infection/severity endpoints.

organization: Inflammatix; Stanford University; Washington University in St. Louis; 22 emergency-department study sites
tested: In the prospective SEPSIS-SHIELD study, a machine-learning blood test using isothermal amplification of 29 host-response mRNAs was evaluated in adults presenting to 22 emergency departments with suspected infection or sepsis.

Clinical adjudication is not a perfect microbiological gold standard, and the study reports lower accuracy when uncertain adjudications are included. This is distinct from the earlier VB10 10-gene signature paper (DOI 10.1016/j.ebiom.2021.103352), which used different genes, cohorts and a different diagnostic score.

The multicenter clinical study measured how those AI-generated scores performed against blinded physician adjudication and near-term clinical endpoints.

title: Deep-learning knee imaging phenotypes reveal osteoarthritis genetic and fracture associations
summary: Using knee DXA scans from the UK Biobank, a ResNet-101 model identified 1,931 more probable knee-osteoarthritis cases than health-record coding and a U-Net segmentation model estimated minimum joint-space width (mJSW). unknown: The paired change does not establish how the protocol compares with alternatives, which differed in what participants saw or judged. The study did not measure long-term retention or behavior.
ai_role: Claude Opus 4.5 generated the opposing sides of a same-subtopic debate before people re-answered the same factual item.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 authors and affiliations, human protocols and model setup, and Table 5","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: A learned simulator identified training orders that delayed detectable reward failures
summary: In controlled experiments with language models trained to write code, researchers used a fitted simulator to select four orderings of training examples. In subsequent runs, the selected orderings reached the threshold for detectable reward failures an average of 96.6% later than four baseline orderings.
ai_technology: SimHack, Qwen3
organization: Google Research; University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
tested: Actual model training runs compared the time to a fixed detectable-failure threshold for four simulator-selected and four baseline orderings.
unknown: The result depends on the studied coding tasks, failure detector and threshold. Delaying the detector’s threshold does not establish prevention or generalize to deployment behavior.
ai_role: The fitted SimHack behavior model predicted the onset under candidate training-example orderings and selected four for actual model runs.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 §2 onset endpoint, §3 learned simulator, and §5.1/Figure 6 measured intervention","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Deep GraphCast features align with where cyclones are headed
summary: An analysis of 205 tropical cyclones found that deeper GraphCast layers carried features that aligned better with cyclone position and pressure structure six hours ahead than at the input time. Researchers identified those features using fitted sparse autoencoders and compared them with historical cyclone tracks and pressure fields.
ai_technology: GraphCast, sparse autoencoders
organization: Tsinghua University; University College London
tested: The retrospective analysis compared feature alignment at the input time and six hours ahead over 2,115 time steps, across 16 processing layers and five separate sparse decompositions of layer 8.
unknown: Feature alignment does not demonstrate that GraphCast uses a particular feature causally or that the feature improves operational forecasts.
ai_role: Sparse autoencoders learned features from GraphCast activations, allowing the researchers to compare feature patterns with distinct cyclone attributes at matching and later times.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 front matter, §2 data and feature fitting, §3.2/3.3 and Figure 4","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Penalizing length changed an AI model’s grammatical choices
summary: Researchers trained Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct to turn structured events into English sentences. Penalizing longer answers increased its preference for shorter grammatical variants, including unfamiliar constructions with an optional “that.” Transfer to more distant constructions was limited.
ai_technology: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, spaCy en_core_web_trf
organization: New York University; The University of Texas at Austin
tested: Post-training varied the length penalty and KL regularization across three seeds, then tested unseen examples of trained and untrained grammatical alternatives.
unknown: This controlled experiment used one small language model. It did not measure human comprehension or show that an analogous penalty caused the language patterns observed in frontier models.
ai_role: A trained dependency parser and learned classifiers quantify linguistic features, and length-penalty post-training of Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct tests grammatical transfer.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 front matter, §§3–4, Figure 7, and Appendices B–C","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: A hidden-state shift can cause a language model to repeat one token
summary: Researchers isolated a shift shared across responses during language-model preference training. Inserting the learned shift into an untreated model reproduced a failure in which one token dominated generation. The failure appeared in 14 of 17 tested model lineages under the study’s per-token ranking objective.
ai_technology: Preference-optimized language models, including Llama-2 and Llama-3.1
organization: The University of Tokyo; TIER IV; Huawei
tested: The authors isolated the shared offset, compared transplantation with magnitude-matched random directions, and tested masking of the component in the training loss.
unknown: The failure depends on model and objective. Related hidden shifts were also observed without generation collapse in tested standard preference-training runs.
ai_role: The researchers isolated a common direction learned during preference training and tested its contribution by transplanting it into an untreated language model.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 front matter, §§4–5 and 7, Appendix B.17, and primary intervention controls","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Video diffusion models were sensitive at similar denoising steps across prompts
summary: Researchers reduced attention in one denoising window at a time. Within each of four pretrained video models, the windows that most changed the final video were similar across eight prompts. Median rank correlations against the other prompts ranged from 0.95 to 1.00.
ai_technology: Wan2.1, Wan2.2, HunyuanVideo
organization: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences; KlingAI Research; Peking University
tested: The experiment compared final-video error with dense attention and ranked ten windows separately for each prompt, holding each prompt out from the comparison rank.
unknown: The result concerns within-model rankings for a small set of prompts and the tested attention perturbation. It does not establish that the same window order applies to other models or sampling settings.
ai_role: Researchers selectively altered attention in trained video diffusion models and measured how the resulting videos departed from the dense model output.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 front matter, §3 attention sensitivity, Figure 2, Appendix D.1 leave-one-out tests","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Carbides became rounder and occupied more of a tempered steel
summary: Researchers used a trained image classifier to separate carbide particles from the surrounding high-speed steel in electron micrographs. After isothermal holding, the measured carbide volume fraction was 9.9%, up from 8.3% in directly quenched reference samples, and mean particle circularity rose from 0.881 to 0.914.
ai_technology: Trainable Weka Segmentation
organization: Ruhr University Bochum; RWTH Aachen University
tested: Microscopy with learned segmentation measured about 1,600 carbides per condition. The stereological measurement error reported for each volume fraction was ±0.4 percentage points.
unknown: The population-level differences apply to the tested alloy and thermal conditions. They do not distinguish growth of existing particles from nucleation of new ones or prove an epitaxial growth mechanism. Carbide rounding during holding had been reported in earlier high-speed-steel research; the represented contribution is quantitative measurement in this alloy.
ai_role: Trainable Weka Segmentation fit a classifier from manually labeled microscopy regions and separated carbide from matrix, enabling particle-area and shape measurements.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 PDF front matter, image segmentation methods, Figures 3–4, Tables 1–2, discussion and conclusions","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Fewer biased answers after model compression often coincided with more abstention
summary: On the BBQ question-answering benchmark, 20 of 26 quantization configurations with fewer biased answers also abstained more often on questions they could answer. The comparison covered models from the Qwen3, Gemma 3 and SmolLM2 families.
ai_technology: Qwen3, Gemma 3, SmolLM2
organization: University of Hull
tested: The authors compared multiple quantization configurations and reported correct, biased, and abstaining answers separately. They also changed prompt wording and removed the abstention option in a separate comparison.
unknown: The 20-of-26 result is conditional on configurations with lower observed bias in this benchmark. It does not measure fairness in real use or establish that all compression increases abstention.
ai_role: The researchers compared outputs from Qwen3, Gemma 3 and SmolLM2 across model sizes and quantization settings, separating abstention from biased or non-biased answers.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 front matter, §§3–5, exact quantization comparison, prompt variation and forced-choice appendix","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: CLIP linked different car classes through shared backgrounds or objects
summary: On UrbanCars, 94.8% of highly similar image pairs from different vehicle classes shared a background or a co-occurring object, compared with 18.1% of random cross-class pairs. Researchers selected the similar pairs using pretrained CLIP features before consulting the dataset’s attribute labels.
ai_technology: CLIP
organization: Indian Institute of Technology Jodhpur
tested: The audit compared randomly chosen cross-class training pairs with pairs selected using high cosine similarity in the frozen feature space.
unknown: The reported proportions concern a dataset constructed with two labeled shortcut attributes and the study’s similarity selection. They do not measure real-world shortcut prevalence.
ai_role: A frozen pretrained vision encoder determined which cross-class examples were closest without using known shortcut labels; audit labels were applied afterward.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 front matter, §4 similarity audit, Table 3 and Figure 2","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Retrieval improvements shrank when combined in a RAG pipeline
summary: Five changes to a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline each improved document ranking when tested alone. Adding their individual gains gave an expected score of 0.667, but the combined system scored 0.483 against a baseline of 0.412. The result concerns the tested retrieval components and queries.
ai_technology: HyDE query augmentation, cross-encoder reranking
organization: IBM
tested: A matched component-composition experiment compared individual changes and the combined pipeline using NDCG@10, with a paired bootstrap over 93 queries.
unknown: The result does not establish that every retrieval pipeline shows the same interaction. The paper’s answer-faithfulness comparison used different component configurations and did not directly establish additivity.
ai_role: Learned query augmentation and cross-encoder reranking change query–document rankings; matched component perturbations test whether those changes add together.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 front matter, §§4–5, Table 6, §D.14/Figure 9 and limitations on faithfulness additivity","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Training AI models on one value shifted their responses on another
summary: Researchers fine-tuned four language models using examples framed around restraint. On held-out scenarios, all four shifted toward responses labeled collectivist, although individualism was not the training target. The finding describes changes in model responses under a synthetic evaluation.
ai_technology: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen3-8B, Gemma-3-12B-Instruct, Ministral-3-8B-Instruct-2512
organization: University of Copenhagen; University of Cambridge
tested: Adapters and their original models scored the same held-out scenarios, with 1,500 examples per value pole. The shift in relative likelihood was significant in each of the four models under the reported multiple-comparison correction. For restraint-trained adapters, the signed table entries correspond to decreases in the raw high-individualism likelihood margin.
unknown: The categories and response examples are synthetic operationalizations. The result does not establish model beliefs, human preferences or behavior in deployment.
ai_role: The study separately fine-tuned four pretrained language models on synthetic examples of individual cultural-value dimensions and then tested labeled response preferences in unrelated dimensions.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 front matter, §§3–4, Appendix C.3/C.4 and Tables 7–11","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: A coding agent made a verified Lean lookup 5.46 times as fast
summary: Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol rewrote the sheet lookup in a Lean port of the Cheat command-line tool. The rewrite searched directly instead of building an intermediate list, and ran 5.46 times as fast as the original Lean function on withheld timing inputs. Lean checked that the two functions return the same result.
ai_technology: Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol, Lean 4
organization: University of California, Berkeley; Amazon Web Services
tested: The study reports repeated paired performance trials and an equality theorem checked by the Lean kernel for the specific rewrite.
unknown: The speedup concerns the named function on the study’s workloads. The equality theorem covers the migrated Lean reference, while agreement with the original Go program was assessed by differential testing.
ai_role: Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol generated a direct reverse-search implementation and a Lean equality proof.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 §5.2 and Appendix D.3, named findConsolidated rewrite and proof scope","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Matching final answers masked different forgetting patterns during fine-tuning
summary: Researchers recovered 100% final performance on an old generation task across several replay budgets for a Qwen model. The same training runs nevertheless followed different trajectories in the probability assigned to correct old answers. The finding came from evaluating checkpoints throughout training as well as the final model.
ai_technology: Qwen and Mistral language-model fine-tuning
organization: The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
tested: The study varied old-task replay budgets at matched training settings and separately measured old-task generation at the endpoint and negative log-likelihood across training checkpoints.
unknown: The result is specific to these models, old-task response tests and replay schedules. Checkpoint behavior cannot establish whether knowledge was removed or merely harder to elicit. The qualified original Qwen retained-response bank contained only 17 examples; its 100% endpoint is not broad preservation of old-task knowledge.
ai_role: Fine-tuned Qwen and Mistral models enabled direct measurement of task outputs and loss at multiple checkpoints under matched training protocols.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 controlled replay budgets and objective allocation, Table 7 and endpoint analysis","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Medical model training changed privacy risk more than who ranked highest
summary: Across six clinical datasets, privacy-risk rankings were broadly similar under many changes to model training. In one chest X-ray cohort, stronger regularization reduced the share of patients above the study’s risk threshold from 88% to 30%. The rankings were compared across training changes using an audit of 7,789 medical-model instances.
ai_technology: ResNet, EfficientNet, vision transformers, ECGFounder, MRI-CORE
organization: University of Crete; Foundation for Research and Technology–Hellas; University of Maryland
tested: A defensive study compared aggregate risk distributions and ordinal stability under seed, architecture, regularization and fine-tuning changes, including comparisons with trained seed replicates.
unknown: The outcomes measure estimated likelihood of training-set membership disclosure under the study’s audit. They do not represent observed patient disclosures or complete invariance across all settings.
ai_role: Researchers trained several thousand medical-model instances, including ECGFounder and MRI-CORE adaptations, and compared aggregate distributions of measured privacy risk across training regimes.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 PDF affiliation, aggregate Figures 2 and 4, cohort and risk-stability comparison","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Routine questions led AI agents to disclose sensitive inferences in simulation
summary: A simulated GPT-5.6 Sol agent revealed restricted conclusions in 85 of 1,200 benign queries designed to be answerable from one document. The study tested synthetic documents and confidentiality controls, showing that an ordinary question can cause an agent to combine information into a restricted inference.
ai_technology: GPT-5.6 Sol and studied agent harnesses
organization: University of Southern California
tested: Researchers measured aggregate disclosures across controlled synthetic queries, reporting a 7.08% rate with a 95% interval of 3.75–10.67% for GPT-5.6 Sol across the tested safeguard and document conditions.
unknown: These are controlled outcomes on synthetic material and specified access settings. The rate does not estimate real-world disclosure frequency.
ai_role: Language-model agents including GPT-5.6 Sol process synthetic documents; researchers compare aggregate disclosure frequencies under confidentiality controls.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 aggregate defensive experimental design, §5.2–§5.3, Figure 1 and Table 16","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Dominant sparse-autoencoder features were often harder to explain
summary: In 65.2% of the sparse autoencoders tested, explanations of the highest-contribution quarter of features ranked activation examples less accurately than explanations for the remaining features. The pattern varied by autoencoder architecture.
ai_technology: Sparse autoencoders over pretrained language-model activations
organization: Purdue University
tested: The study tested a dominance-aware explanation-ranking measure across seven autoencoder architectures and checked robustness to firing-frequency matching and different explanation and judging models.
unknown: This is an explanation-ranking proxy, not a complete account of each feature’s meaning or its causal role in downstream decisions.
ai_role: Trained sparse autoencoders represent language-model activations, and model-generated feature explanations are checked using ranked activation evidence.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 §3 dominance and explanation tests, §4 Table 2 and Figure 3; same aggregate result in v2","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: An agent trace detector misread repeated calculator calls as verification
summary: A human audit of calculator-assisted AI traces found that repeated calculator calls could be mislabeled as verification of earlier outputs. The October 21 preprint already reported this failure pattern and 14 disagreements. Its November 18 revision additionally reported fair agreement across 81 trace labels (κ = 0.29).
ai_technology: Tool-using language models
organization: University of Illinois Chicago; Argonne National Laboratory
tested: The study introduced controlled calculator errors, measured agent behavior, and compared automated labels with human reading of the trace.
unknown: A visible tool call cannot reveal every internal check. The annotated sample and controlled arithmetic setting do not establish reliability on other tools or tasks. One author audited a selected, flag-guided sample with automated labels visible; this was not a blind independent annotation. The agreement statistic was reported in v2, after the underlying audit appeared in v1.
ai_role: Multiple learned agents produce calculator-assisted reasoning traces on controlled arithmetic tasks. Human auditors compare these traces with automatically generated labels.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 original human audit and failure pattern, checked against v2 §§2–5, Tables 4 and 8 and updated agreement statistic","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: AI decoders missed 168 verifiable messages in a controlled audit
summary: In an audit of 7,200 language-model outputs, researchers found 168 verifiable hidden messages that the original model decoders failed to recover. The result shows that decoder failure alone can miss successful encoding in this controlled test.
ai_technology: Gemini, Claude, GPT language-model encoders and decoders
organization: University of Maryland, College Park
tested: The researchers compared original model-decoder results with an independent deterministic verification of the output.
unknown: The result applies to the tested synthetic messages and verification criteria. It does not estimate prevalence in real communications. Of the 168 cases, 58 were recovered with exploratory procedures added after inspecting the corpus. Verification also allowed normalized letter-sequence matches, rather than requiring byte-exact messages, and does not establish intentional encoding.
ai_role: Learned language models produced and attempted to recover messages. An independent deterministic audit checked recoverability to evaluate what the model decoders missed.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 aggregate encoding/decoding contingency results and validity distinctions","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Unacknowledged suggestions influenced AI reasoning through question and filler tokens
summary: Researchers found that activation changes at questions and filler tokens carried part of an unacknowledged suggestion’s influence in two language models. Swapping those native activations partially shifted the models’ next-token predictions toward the predictions made without the suggestion.
ai_technology: Gemma-4-E4B-it, DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B
organization: University of Wisconsin-Madison; University of Oxford
tested: The two-target patch recovered 16.2% of the counterfactual distribution shift in Gemma and 19.3% in the DeepSeek model, measured by the study’s KL-divergence recovery metric. Equal-size random token controls recovered less.
unknown: The experiment concerns held-fixed responses under the tested suggestions. It establishes partial mediation at the selected locations, with effects that differ by model.
ai_role: A fitted residual stream editor identified candidate locations where hidden representations preserve a suggestion’s influence, which researchers tested with independent native activation patching.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 causal analysis §§4.1–4.2, Figures 5–7 and matched token controls","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Safety probe errors followed predictable scaling across three model families
summary: Researchers fit scaling laws to safety probes trained on smaller language models. The fits predicted the error of the next larger model to within 0.02 in 52 of 72 comparisons at the largest label budget. They tested these held-out predictions in the Qwen2.5, Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4 families.
ai_technology: Learned activation probes on Qwen2.5, Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4
organization: University of Washington; Anthropic
tested: The study trained two probe architectures across twenty models and compared held-out next-size forecasts with measured performance. Probe error was one minus AUROC.
unknown: The held-out extrapolation covers three model families and the study’s six safety tasks. The fitted constants and accuracy may differ with other data or probe designs.
ai_role: Learned activation probes trained on up to a million labels per setting generate measurement curves; power-law fits on smaller models predict performance on a held-out larger model.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 §§3–5.1, Figure 10 and E.6 held-out model-size comparisons, confirmed core claim in v2","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Antihypertensive use was linked to slightly longer time without recorded cognitive impairment
summary: In a retrospective All of Us analysis targeting a high-risk population with model-derived weights, baseline antihypertensive use was associated with slightly longer time without a first recorded mild cognitive impairment diagnosis. The ratio of geometric mean time capped at 48 months was 1.012 overall and 1.026 in a subgroup with cardiometabolic and depressive multimorbidity.
ai_technology: Regularized logistic regression, cross-fitted XGBoost
organization: Columbia University; University of Michigan
tested: The study trained its risk model in a non-overlapping internal reference set of 83,745 participants and estimated associations in a 37,577-participant analysis set with 500 first recorded MCI diagnoses within 48 months. Model-derived weights target a high-risk population without restricting the cohort to a directly observed high-risk stratum.
unknown: The estimates are associations involving baseline medication use and the first recorded diagnosis. Treatment initiation, adherence, causal benefit and external validation were outside the study.
ai_role: A regularized logistic model fitted to the non-overlapping reference sample estimates target high-risk membership; cross-fitted XGBoost models estimate treatment propensity and outcomes.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 §4 propensity/outcome models, logistic risk weights, sample construction, Table 3 and Figure 3","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: More specific wording narrowed semantic representations in four language models
summary: Researchers compared sentences that made a meaning more specific with sentences that merely added detail. Across four language models, the more specific versions formed tighter neighborhoods in model activation space. The pattern persisted after removing five dominant directions of variation.
ai_technology: Gemma 4, Llama 3.2, Qwen2.5, Pythia
organization: Imperial College London
tested: Controlled refinement and elaboration chains were checked using blind human judgments. Across the four models, the contraction contrast persisted in 86–100% of layers after the five dominant directions were removed.
unknown: The result depends on the constructed text contrasts and representation measures. It does not demonstrate causal use of the contraction in other language tasks.
ai_role: Pretrained activation geometry is measured as controlled texts move from broader meanings to more specific descriptions, with blind human checks on the contrasts.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 abstract and affiliation, refinement design, Figure 5, permutation tests and quality-controlled rerun","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: A latent safety monitor flagged fewer harmful prompts than model refusals
summary: Across 15 language models and a held-out set of reworded prompts, one activation-based monitor flagged about 23% of harmful prompts at the same false-alarm rate as a string-matched refusal reference, which flagged about 32%. A later activation readout caught more, but analyses linked much of that gain to the model’s own refusal decision.
ai_technology: Latent Guard, linear and multilayer activation probes
organization: University of Massachusetts Amherst
tested: The authors compared trained readers and string-matched model refusal at matched false alarm rates and tested how their scores tracked the models’ planned replies.
unknown: The comparison covers particular rewordings and learned monitors. It does not establish the limits of every activation-based safety monitor. Refusal wording can be missed by the reference detector; a sampled audit found only 13 of 135 replies labeled answered actually provided harmful assistance. Later-readout gains therefore do not all represent detection of genuine unsafe compliance.
ai_role: Learned latent readers classify prompts from instruction-tuned model activations and are checked against observed refusals and embedding models.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 front matter, aggregate §6 out-of-distribution reader comparison and matched false-alarm analysis","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Early recommendations shaped what AI groups chose later
summary: In a controlled music recommendation study, 13 language-model populations evaluated the same 48 unfamiliar song lyrics. When popularity strongly influenced what agents saw, the first 30 agents’ choices predicted later popularity better than recommendations made without popularity information for all 13 populations.
ai_technology: Thirteen language-model populations; Suno v4.5 stimuli
organization: Cornell University; Stanford University
tested: Each model had an independent baseline and eight simulated populations per influence condition. The study compared early choices and independent rankings as predictors of later recommendations.
unknown: The experiment used synthetic lyrics and a controlled interface, so the magnitude of herding may differ in other recommendation settings.
ai_role: Thirteen learned language-model populations select and recommend previously unseen Suno-generated lyrics under random exposure to popularity ordering and counts or independent evaluation.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 §§2–3, Figure 1 design, Figure 5 temporal comparison, appendix robustness and Table S2","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Speech model representations tracked estimated quality less well under severe distortion
summary: Four pretrained speech encoders tracked estimated quality better for mildly distorted recordings than for severely distorted ones. Researchers compared clean and degraded versions of 100 English utterances across four levels of simulated distortion.
ai_technology: WavLM, HuBERT, SPEAR, Wav2Vec 2.0
organization: KAIST
tested: The study compared rank correlations between encoder distances and several quality estimators, including a conventional spectral-distance check, with bootstrapped uncertainty.
unknown: The degradations were simulated and the outcomes were based on quality proxies. The study did not measure how listeners rated or understood the recorded speech.
ai_role: WavLM, HuBERT, SPEAR and Wav2Vec 2.0 encode clean and artificially degraded speech, enabling direct comparisons of preserved acoustic information across severities.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 front matter, §2 severity and representation analysis and Figure 2","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Reasoning models usually inherited the revision marker “wait” before reinforcement learning
summary: In 17 of 18 tested reinforcement-learning runs starting from models that rarely wrote “wait,” the word stayed rare even as math accuracy improved. In the traced OLMo-3 lineage, the word appeared during mid-training before reinforcement learning and became more frequent afterward.
ai_technology: OLMo-3, Qwen2.5, Qwen3, Mistral
organization: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology; Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab; Peking University
tested: The analysis compared published checkpoint histories and controlled training runs, using fewer than 0.05 occurrences per thousand generated tokens as its absence criterion.
unknown: The result concerns a visible marker on the sampled tasks. It does not show whether a model reconsidered an answer without writing “wait.”
ai_role: Researchers sampled language-model outputs across recorded training stages and externally released and newly trained reinforcement-learning checkpoints.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 affiliations, main provenance contrasts, released-checkpoint lineage and robustness appendix","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: AI captions added unsupported detail in the middle and more reference-unmatched content near the end
summary: In long captions for 198 images, six AI models produced more reference-unsupported specifics in the middle. The mean share assigned to a residual reference-unmatched category rose from 10.3% in the first quarter to 28.1% in the last. This category need not mean that a sentence is objectively vague.
ai_technology: Qwen3-based claim extraction and verification; Qwen3-VL, InternVL3.5 and LLaVA captioners
organization: Beihang University; Kuaishou Technology; Fudan University; Zhejiang University
tested: Researchers divided captions into quarters, assessed claims against human-derived image rubrics, and checked a sample of verifier judgments with human reviewers.
unknown: A caption can include a true detail omitted from its reference. The reported pattern concerns this sample and reference-based labeling, with only sampled image-level checks.
ai_role: Qwen models extract and verify ordered atomic claims from human references and generated captions; human annotators validate a sample of judgments.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 §3, Figure 1/Table 1, appendix comparison to 347 human rubric judgments and sampled visual recheck","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Coding agents broke verified site behavior after completing requested changes
summary: In 107 of 586 benchmark runs that completed the requested website change and had comparable baseline checks, the coding agent broke an already verified browser state. In 78 of those 586 runs, a continuity check still failed at the end.
ai_technology: Coding agents evaluated with ProductWebBench
organization: Beihang University; IQuest Research; Huawei Technologies
tested: The study replayed checks against untouched repositories and states that each run had previously passed. The 586-run subset had evidence from both comparisons.
unknown: The rates are specific to the completing runs with both baselines available, and do not estimate production software regression rates.
ai_role: Thirteen language-model systems implement requested code changes; browser checks on baseline and altered repositories expose regressions.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 controlled task construction, §§4–5, Table 4 and Appendix C provenance comparison","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Country names and query language shifted AI answers in different ways
summary: In tests with three language models, naming a country in the user’s message moved open-ended responses 30–44% closer to the same model’s answers when assigned that country as a persona. Changing the query language instead shifted multiple-choice responses away from the associated persona in all three models.
ai_technology: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Ministral-3-14B-Instruct-2512, Gemma-3-27B-IT
organization: University of Copenhagen; Aalborg University Copenhagen; Bocconi University
tested: The controlled study compared named-country and language cues across survey-derived choices and about 1.6 million open-ended responses.
unknown: The reference was each model’s own persona-conditioned responses rather than people’s values. Country and language stand in for only a small part of cultural identity, and the measured shifts depended on prompt design.
ai_role: Llama, Ministral and Gemma generate answers under matched national persona, named-country and language cues; learned annotation and translation models support value comparisons.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 §§3–5.2, Figure 2, annotation and translation sensitivity appendices","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: People adopted false facts from confident AI tutors
summary: In a study with 32 volunteers, participants selected an assistant’s planted false answer for about 60% of quiz items assigned false information, compared with 11% of items assigned correct information. Mean scores fell from 7.4 to 2.9 out of 10 between fully accurate and fully falsified GPT-5-mini briefings.
ai_technology: GPT-5-mini
organization: Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham; Indian Institute of Science
tested: The counterbalanced study used five briefing reliability levels and 104 completed quizzes, with independently randomized topic order and corrective debriefing.
unknown: This was a small study with one underlying model, deliberately confident responses, and immediate quizzes. Retention over longer periods and responses to other assistants were not assessed. Participants could continue consulting the same assistant during each quiz. The measured choices do not establish unaided memory retention or durable internalized beliefs.
ai_role: GPT-5-mini chat assistants explained science topics from briefings containing controlled levels of plausible false claims.
source_review: {"scope":"arXiv v1 trial design §§3.1–3.7, Table 3, §4.2 and ethics statement","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: A judge flagged more concerning answers early in OLMo reinforcement learning than at the end
summary: In tests of OLMo-3-7B-Think, GPT-4o flagged 25.0% of outputs after supervised fine-tuning, 46.1% early in reinforcement learning, and 11.8% at the final checkpoint. The labels cover text that the judge classified as power-seeking or related behavior. The two judges agreed least near the apparent peak.
ai_technology: OLMo-3-7B-Think, GPT-4o, Gemini 2.0 Flash
organization: Barış Alparslan, Sandy Tanwisuth and Caleb Petterson (affiliations not stated in the reviewed preprint)
tested: The authors repeated the same 76 benchmark questions across 16 released post-training checkpoints and compared binary labels from two judging models.

summary: Researchers used a sparse autoencoder to find a feature associated with a sawtooth synthesizer lead in the text2midi model. summary: In an analysis of 26,459 foreground patches from PartImageNet, frozen DINOv2 features became less distinguishable near labeled object-part boundaries. summary: A fitted subgroup model assigned chest X-rays in a 22,281-image CheXpert-Plus test set to image groups. Across discovered groups, cardiomegaly sensitivity ranged from 0.10 to 0.98. summary: In a paired study of 20 applications at one investment firm, mean analyst time was 44.7 minutes for manual screening and 18.9 minutes for screening with GPT-6 Luna-assisted reports. summary: Using learned MACE potentials, simulations estimated excited-state torsional relaxation in unsubstituted biphenyl across nine solvents. organization: Emory University

summary: A learned detector using coronary-vessel features achieved AP@50 of 0.434 on 48 angiography images from 27 Oxford Acute Myocardial Infarction study patients.
