ai_technology: Claude Opus 5.5; Qwen3-Coder; Nemotron Cascade 2
organization: Independent researcher
tested: A secondary offline diagnostic applied selected generated artifacts unchanged to fresh task copies, bypassing only strict parameter-name comparison, then ran the original sealed behavioral checks. No parent review or end-to-end acceptance was replayed.
unknown: This selected subset cannot estimate overall pass rates or establish that contract requirements were unnecessary in deployment. Original saved records were private and not independently auditable; passing these author-supplied checks does not prove general software correctness.
ai_role: Existing language models acting as coding workers generated artifacts assessed under an interface contract and hidden behavioral tests.
source_review: {"scope":"v1 §§9.3–9.4 coding delegation and post hoc hidden-test diagnostic","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Simulated robots sometimes completed tasks while violating safety requirements
summary: In controlled simulations across six manipulation tasks, 82 valid executions completed their tasks while violating at least one separately checked safety rule. The tests evaluated learned ACT and RDT control policies under deliberately introduced faults. Counts refer to simulated executions in a focused test campaign.
ai_technology: ACT; RDT robotic manipulation policies; EAST digital-twin testing
organization: Macau University of Science and Technology; Beihang University; University of Nottingham Ningbo China; Swinburne University of Technology
tested: Five campaigns used the simulator to verify that test conditions occurred and evaluated task completion separately from predefined safety requirements.
unknown: The cases may share tasks and scenarios. This fault-focused simulation does not estimate physical incident rates. Earlier safety benchmarks already reported successful-but-unsafe robot trajectories; this result is a further specific policy/task validation, not discovery of that general gap.
ai_role: Two learned manipulation policy families, ACT and RDT, produced execution traces in which task completion and predefined safety rules were evaluated separately.
source_review: {"scope":"v1 design, independent runtime outcome checks, equal-budget campaigns and unsafe-success results","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Language models flagged missing evidence less often when an unsupported premise was usable
summary: In paired arithmetic tasks, making an unsupported premise usable reduced missing-evidence flags by 8–30 percentage points across four tested language models. The source support was unchanged. Some answers may reflect conditional reasoning because the instructions did not require rejection of premises supplied in the question.
ai_technology: Gemma and Qwen language models
organization: Google
tested: The controlled factorial design varied actionability and the mention of relevant entities on GSM8K. All 16 primary paired contrasts survived Holm adjustment.
unknown: The selected tasks and instructions limit how broadly the result applies. It does not show that all answers accept unsupported statements as facts. Pattern-based scoring was revised after a 40-response audit; residual condition-dependent scoring error was not bounded by that small check.
ai_role: Four pretrained Gemma and Qwen language models answered mathematically matched prompts with equally unsupported premises that varied in usability.
source_review: {"scope":"v1 Methods, paired premise design, §4 and Limitations","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: A learned prover exposed ambiguous translations of unique-answer math problems
summary: A learned prover found two distinct Lean-accepted answers for 5.4% of the tested formal statements pooled across three autoformalizers. The original problems had unique answers, so these examples expose a mismatch between the formal statements and their intended problems.
ai_technology: Gobble-Prover 1.7B and 4B; Lean 4
organization: University of California, Riverside
tested: The audit combined evidence from two learned provers across three autoformalizers and five contest problem datasets. Lean checked acceptance of distinct answers.
unknown: The detected rate is a lower bound for these tested versions. A translation can be wrong in ways this multiple-answer test does not flag.
ai_role: Gobble-Prover models generated verifiable proof terms for numerical candidates under independently autoformalized competition problems.
source_review: {"scope":"v1 Methods, unique-answer argument, Appendix D Table 5","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Successful human puzzle players voiced qualitative explanations more often than language agents
summary: In an ARC-AGI-3 trajectory study, qualitative descriptions appeared in 72 of 144 successful human runs and 17 of 119 successful runs from three agent systems. The human data came from think-aloud recordings and the model data from agent traces. The comparison measures recorded descriptions in successfully completed games.
ai_technology: GPT-5.6 Sol assisted analysis; ARC-AGI-3 agent traces
organization: Nanyang Technological University; Technical University of Darmstadt; Basis Research Institute; Harvard University; Cornell University
tested: The authors collected 144 human trajectories across 64 participants and 25 games, collected 250 publicly released model trajectories, and analyzed successful subsets. They spot-checked parts of the model-assisted annotation.
unknown: Differences in what humans say aloud and what agents write or log limit claims about underlying cognitive representations.
ai_role: GPT-5.6 Sol implemented trigger detectors and annotated cognition from aligned transcripts and game traces. Learned agent trajectories supplied matched-task comparison material.
source_review: {"scope":"v1 annotation workflow, participant selection, Section 4 trajectory results","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: An intrinsically trained fly model matched an observed future-turn signal
summary: Among 20 intrinsic learning objectives, DIAYN produced virtual fly policies that most closely matched the relationship between neural and behavioral prediction of future turns in prior fruit-fly recordings. The comparison evaluated signals 15 to 8 seconds before a turn. It supports a computational model of the observed behavior.
ai_technology: DIAYN; NeuroMechFly; elastic-net logistic decoding
organization: University of Maryland, College Park; Carnegie Mellon University
tested: The researchers held the digital embodiment and comparison assay consistent while varying intrinsic learning objectives and comparing frozen policies with prior aggregate observations.
unknown: The behavior and neural comparisons test a simulated model. They do not establish that live flies optimize the same objective. The comparison selected among 20 objectives and seven candidate internal representations; decoder hyperparameters were tuned on the biological data. Agreement is not an untouched validation of a uniquely identified biological objective.
ai_role: DIAYN and other learned intrinsic-motivation algorithms train hierarchical policies. Fitted elastic-net decoders compare future-turn information in the models and prior fly recordings.
source_review: {"scope":"v1 policy comparison, prospective decoding Figure 3 and Results","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Later attention queries rescued selected early-loop retrieval errors
summary: Moving same-item later-loop attention queries into the first loop corrected 89.8% and 96.9% of selected synthetic two-hop errors in two Ouro models. Queries shuffled between items corrected 23.7% and 20.6%, respectively. The result applies to questions answered incorrectly in the first loop and correctly later.
ai_technology: Ouro-1.4B; Ouro-2.6B; activation transplantation
organization: University of British Columbia
tested: The primary synthetic test included 600 scenes per model, with 245 and 223 qualifying early-loop errors, respectively. Same-item and shuffled queries were compared at aligned positions.
unknown: Natural-question rescue was smaller and did not establish bridge redirection. A positional contribution remains possible. In Ouro-1.4B the rescue changes four-candidate ranking, not greedy generated answers. The intervention supplies a separate query at every layer/head, not one vector; the two model sizes share developmental history.
ai_role: The authors intervened on pretrained Ouro attention query activations and compared matched late-loop and shuffled donors.
source_review: {"scope":"v1 query swap Methods, Table 2 and natural-question caveats","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: An audit found errors in screened AI-extracted electro-optic values
summary: A curated-reference audit found that 30 of 112 electro-optic records extracted with GPT-4o and accepted by automated checks were defective. Errors included incorrect tensor components, units and measurement conditions. The audit covered three selected legacy papers and does not estimate error rates for the full database.
ai_technology: GPT-4o; materials literature extraction
organization: New Jersey Institute of Technology; University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
tested: The audit reviewed records already accepted by the extraction pipeline against curated source information and physical consistency checks.
unknown: These papers were selected as a stress test. Different formats and data complexity could yield different error rates.
ai_role: GPT-4o extracted reported electro-optic property values and contexts from primary documents for database construction.
source_review: {"scope":"primary v1-only PDF §§3 and 5.2, production audit and source comparison","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Inferring driver intent increased aligned steering assistance in a simulator study
summary: In an urban driving simulator, 8 of 11 participants with paired observations received more steering assistance aligned with their intent under the intent-conditioned policy. Collisions occurred in 4 of 147 intent-conditioned trials, 10 of 130 trials with assistance lacking intent inference, and 2 of 121 unassisted trials.
ai_technology: Dream2Assist; recurrent state-space world model; reinforcement learning
organization: Toyota Research Institute
tested: Participants experienced within-subject simulator trials under intent-conditioned, non-intent, and unassisted conditions in randomized order. Physical driving was only a preliminary deployment.
unknown: Trial counts are repeated within people and collisions were concentrated among a few participants. The measurements do not establish an on-road safety benefit.
ai_role: A trained recurrent world model infers driver intent and conditions the assistance policy. The same architectural comparator omits the intent predictor.
source_review: {"scope":"v1 urban simulator human study, §6.4 objective results and preliminary on-vehicle scope","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Agents reversed fewer correct judgments when they recorded evidence before feedback
summary: Across 75 passing draft evaluations, five Gemini models reversed a correct decision in 41 standard trials and 34 trials when the models wrote a claim checklist after feedback. The full pre-feedback checklist condition recorded 9 reversals. The test used a fixed set of deliberately mistaken critiques.
ai_technology: Gemini language models; controlled claim and feedback ordering
organization: Google
tested: A controlled report-review study compared the order of evidential self-assessment and feedback, with 20 scenarios per model and separate cases containing valid correction.
unknown: Scenario and model dependence matter: the same scenarios were reused and the benchmark uses selected passing or flawed drafts.
ai_role: Five Gemini models reevaluated their reports, with the timing of recording earlier claims varied around identical mistaken criticism.
source_review: {"scope":"v1 controlled Turn-2 report review, §4.3 Table 3 and evaluation limits","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Layers important to LoRA adaptation varied across tasks
summary: In an intervention study on fine-tuned Qwen2.5-0.5B, the seven layers most important to adaptation had a mean pairwise overlap of 39.5% by the Jaccard measure across four tasks. Only the first three layers appeared in every top-seven list.
ai_technology: Qwen2.5-0.5B; low-rank adaptation; activation path patching
organization: East China Normal University; Brunel University of London
tested: The intervention compares layer-level learned contributions, then ranks the layers separately for the four task datasets.
unknown: The overlap depends on selected datasets, model, rankings and layer cutoff. It does not establish identical sparsity across architectures.
ai_role: Path patching intervened on learned LoRA activations to measure each layer’s contribution on four datasets.
source_review: {"scope":"Qwen2.5-0.5B four-dataset path-patching Methods and Figure 3","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Judge-labeled invalid coding traces were longer in two related models
summary: Code-generation reasoning traces labeled invalid by a model-judge ensemble averaged 17,163 tokens for DeepSeek-R1-0528, compared with 7,102 for valid-labeled traces. Its distilled 8B variant showed the same direction. These labels concern reasoning coherence and are explicitly distinct from whether the final code passes functional tests.
ai_technology: DeepSeek-R1-0528; DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B
organization: Shanghai Jiao Tong University
tested: Researchers collected traces under matched prompting and decoding. Three model judges each rated trace validity three times; confidence-weighted votes labeled high-confidence cases and two human annotators adjudicated the remainder. The reported length contrast groups these trace-validity labels, not final code correctness.
unknown: Validity judgments include coherence and unnecessary detours, which may themselves relate to trace length; the contrast does not establish a causal effect of long reasoning or a functional-code failure rate. The models share a lineage, selected complete traces exclude incomplete or unparsable responses, and verbal traces need not faithfully reflect internal reasoning.
ai_role: DeepSeek R1 models generated traces; DeepSeek-V3.2, Gemini-3-Flash and GLM-5.1 judged their validity, while learned semantic annotators classified reasoning actions.
source_review: {"scope":"v1 task/model setup, trace taxonomy and §§4.1–4.2 differences by outcome","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Calibrated spin models better matched a measured diamond ensemble spectrum
summary: For a measured zero-field nitrogen-vacancy ensemble spectrum, calibrating effective spin-model terms reduced held-frequency error from 0.008835 to 0.003872 across four folds. The source models were learned from single-center spectra, and both comparisons fitted the same linewidth and optical-readout terms.
ai_technology: Symbolic regression; learned effective spin Hamiltonians
organization: University of New South Wales; Cryo-X Tech; Xidian University
tested: The authors used a matched comparison across held frequencies in a 38-point experimental scan and froze each learned source expression before fitting the target ensemble.
unknown: Other effective compositions can produce comparable spectra, so this does not uniquely determine microscopic parameters. The independent field-condition test reported elsewhere in the paper uses simulation.
ai_role: Constrained symbolic regression selected and fitted spin Hamiltonian models from measured single-center spectra. The models formed the starting point for ensemble calibration.
source_review: {"scope":"primary v1-only PDF learned source models and Section IV experimental ensemble fits","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Language models missed more requirements with little wording in common with the final request
summary: Across 405 CL-bench Life tasks, direct answers from four language models passed 67.4% of rubric criteria with low wording overlap with the final request, compared with 81.1% of higher-overlap criteria. The analysis uses word overlap as a proxy and does not establish that wording alone caused the difference.
ai_technology: GPT-6 Luna; Kimi K3; Grok 4.7; GLM-5
organization: The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Macao Polytechnic University; The Hong Kong Polytechnic University
tested: The study grouped 5,333 classifiable rubric criteria by overlap with the final request. The evaluators assessed individual outputs under the benchmark rubric.
unknown: Groups can differ in underlying difficulty and scoring criteria. Rubrics are nested within tasks, and the result does not establish effects in live workflows.
ai_role: Four frozen language models generated corpus-task answers. A rubric judge scored outputs from the same benchmark before testing the proposed harness.
source_review: {"scope":"v1 CL-bench Life task corpus description, lexical rubric groups and direct-answer results","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Parkinson’s connectivity retrieval found similarly mixed neighbors for cases and controls
summary: Among 40 participants in the TaoWu cohort, the ten closest matches in a learned connectivity representation were 79.5% Parkinson’s cases for diagnosed participants and 81.0% for controls, on average. The source pool included 139 people with Parkinson’s among 169 participants. Retrieval did not consistently improve classification beyond pretraining alone.
ai_technology: Graph convolutional autoencoder; functional-connectivity retrieval
organization: Carl von Ossietzky University of Oldenburg
tested: A frozen encoder was trained on external cohorts. The researchers summarized matched neighbor labels and compared prediction variants using repeated cross-validation in the separate TaoWu cohort.
unknown: The study is small and the source lookup is label-imbalanced. Same-fold checkpoint selection and cohort differences limit interpretation of classification metrics.
ai_role: A graph convolutional autoencoder learned functional-connectivity embeddings from 169 external individuals. Neighbor identities and a downstream classifier evaluated a separate 40-person sample.
source_review: {"scope":"v1 cohort Methods, Table 1 and Figure 2 controls; PDF author affiliation","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Rank compression followed delayed generalization in tested Transformers
summary: In 29 one-layer Transformer runs that developed delayed generalization on modular arithmetic, the steepest effective-rank drop followed the rise in test accuracy by about 900 training steps. In a separate intervention, restricting embedding rank prevented delayed generalization in 15 of 20 runs.
ai_technology: One-layer Transformers; rank-constrained training
organization: Lossfunk
tested: The paper used a predefined test-accuracy threshold and compared rank restrictions with factorized full-rank models across seeds.
unknown: Results concern small arithmetic models. Timing and intervention findings do not exclude other roles for representation compression in other training regimes.
ai_role: Trained modular-arithmetic Transformers and matched factorized controls serve as instruments for evaluating weight rank and generalization timing.
source_review: {"scope":"v1 one-layer Transformer results, rank intervention and Appendix E","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: An AI-assisted audit found eight maintainer-confirmed software regressions
summary: An audit of 1,459 merged pull requests in four Python projects used language models to generate behavior checks. The study found nine reproducible regression candidates, of which eight were confirmed by maintainers. The result concerns a targeted software audit.
ai_technology: ORION; learned test generation and behavioral oracles
organization: Beihang University; National University of Singapore
tested: ORION flagged 28 requests. The authors retained and manually reviewed currently reproducible warnings before submitting nine candidates for maintainer confirmation.
unknown: The reviewers did not comprehensively assess unflagged changes, so recall and general defect rates are unknown. This is not a count of security vulnerabilities.
ai_role: ORION uses a learned model to infer intended software behavior and generate checks for regression candidates in existing projects.
source_review: {"scope":"v1 ORION design and §V-E real-world regression evaluation","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: AI reviewers favored confident wording in matched research papers
summary: In a 504-paper experiment, all six model reviewers more often gave higher scores to rewrites with confident wording. Claude Sonnet 4.6 favored the confident version in 40% of pairs and the less confident version in 6%, with 54% tied. Researchers checked text similarity and wording shifts before comparing evaluations.
ai_technology: Claude Sonnet 4.6; GPT-5.5; Gemini; Gemma; Qwen; GLM
organization: CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security; German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence; University of Technology Nuremberg; Inria
tested: Each model independently evaluated one rewrite at a time for each pair under standardized review instructions. The study checked style manipulation and content similarity on the rewritten manuscripts.
unknown: Rewriting can introduce small uncontrolled meaning changes. The experiment concerns model scores and does not measure actual conference decisions.
ai_role: Language models generated matched high- and low-confidence prose variants and six model reviewers independently scored the rewritten versions.
source_review: {"scope":"v1 paired rewrite checks and 504-paper comparative review experiment, Table 4","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Symbolic regression fitted a finite-Reynolds-number correction for turbulent velocity profiles
summary: A data-fitted expression adjusted the outer wake contribution in zero-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layers as Reynolds number varied. The mean-velocity relation was compared with 35 simulation and experiment profiles across friction Reynolds numbers from 252 to 72,526. Its high-Reynolds-number limit was imposed during modeling.
ai_technology: PySR; physics-constrained symbolic regression
organization: Chinese Academy of Sciences; Northwestern Polytechnical University
tested: The authors identified the fitted correction from specified direct- and large-eddy-simulation profiles and compared the relation with other profiles including experimental datasets.
unknown: Out-of-fit profiles were not an independent statistical validation set. The limiting value is a design constraint, and reported data sources differ in the outer layer.
ai_role: PySR fit near-wall and finite-Reynolds-number corrections under prescribed physical asymptotes.
source_review: {"scope":"v1 reference datasets, symbolic-regression implementation and Sections 4.1–4.2","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: A vision-assisted drone tracked moving pipes in a physical test
summary: In a physical moving-pipe test, a small drone using learned visual label detection and a model-predictive controller recorded 6.73% average tracking error, compared with 15.13% under a standard PID controller. The study compared control methods in a bounded experimental rig.
ai_technology: YOLOv5; learned visual label detection; model predictive control
organization: Northwestern Polytechnical University; Shanghai Jiao Tong University
tested: The study used a Tello drone to compare controller behavior in three lab scenarios, with camera-based detection feeding position estimates.
unknown: This tests the integrated labeled setup under controlled conditions and does not establish field inspection reliability or collision reduction.
ai_role: YOLOv5 detects visual pipe labels so that both feedback designs can estimate relative position.
source_review: {"scope":"v1 learned perception Methods and matched Tello experiments, Table III","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Both driving models detected the other vehicle before most simulated collisions
summary: On the NeuroNCAP simulator, object tracking met the study’s detection criterion before 95.9% of DiffusionDrive’s collisions and 95.8% of SparseDrive’s collisions. The audit distinguished missed actors from collision episodes in which the learned detection system had tracked the actor.
ai_technology: DiffusionDrive and SparseDrive, learned vehicle detection and planning
organization: University of Stuttgart; Mercedes-Benz
tested: The authors separated stock-model simulation episodes by collision outcome and by whether vehicle tracking met a prespecified analysis criterion.
unknown: The result depends on the simulator, models and tracking definition. The presence of a detection does not identify the cause of an individual crash or establish road performance.
ai_role: The learned perception systems provided the actor tracks compared with closed-loop simulation outcomes.
source_review: {"scope":"§IV.A–B, Table I and front matter","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Eight learned streamflow models underestimated peak days in a basin audit
summary: A 162-basin evaluation found median peak-day biases of 27% to 44% below observed flow across eight learned models, versus 13% below for the National Water Model. The learned models also underestimated peak days in a broader analysis of 1,139 basins.
ai_technology: LSTM, GRU, EA-LSTM and five other learned streamflow models
organization: Rutgers University; Apple; University of Alabama; University of Maryland
tested: Models trained through water year 2010 were scored against recorded streamflow over 2011–2022. Bias was summarized over basins.
unknown: Model tuning and inputs were constrained. The external National Water Model used its developers’ calibration, which may overlap the test period. Flow estimates at extremes carry observational uncertainty.
ai_role: Eight models learned mappings from weather history and basin attributes to daily streamflow; their held-out errors revealed the common peak-day deficit.
source_review: {"scope":"§§3–4.2, Tables 1–2 and front matter","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Tactile guidance improved immediate racket-skill ratings in a randomized study
summary: After ten minutes of practice, 12 learners given contact and motion guidance improved by 0.72 levels on a four-level expert rating scale. Twelve learners who received only proficiency-level feedback gained 0.05 levels. The difference was 0.67 levels (95% confidence interval 0.39 to 0.98).
ai_technology: GNN–LSTM pose estimator; graph-informed drive–grip encoder and decoder
organization: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
tested: A separate cohort of 24 was randomly assigned to equal-duration practice. Three experts rated shuffled before-and-after clips without labels identifying the group or assessment time.
unknown: This small study evaluated immediate changes on five racket skills. Durability and transfer to match play were unestablished.
ai_role: A learned pose estimator reconstructed contact geometry from tactile input. Learned control representations and regional analysis informed feedback on how each learner’s contact and timing differed from an expert reference.
source_review: {"scope":"Front matter; hand–racket reconstruction, control organization, mechanism-guided learning, and Supplementary Notes 14–16","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: A certified input extends a lower bound for qubit-channel capacity
summary: An AI-assisted search found a 45-qubit input with positive coherent information at per-Pauli error probability 0.064966. The author used the prior certifier unchanged, extending the earlier certified point of 0.064956. This gives a lower bound for where the depolarizing channel can transmit quantum information.
ai_technology: Claude Sonnet 5.5; Infinity Machine research agent
organization: Harish Santhanalakshmi Ganesan, independent researcher
tested: Exact arithmetic enclosed coherent information between 2.31 and 2.78 × 10⁻⁸ bits. The total Pauli error probability is three times the per-Pauli probability.
unknown: The bound applies to the supplied input. The optimal threshold is unknown, and the cited author check does not establish independent confirmation.
ai_role: Claude Sonnet 5.5 wrote and ran an optimizer starting with an earlier witness. The human operator supplied the task, seed and verification tools.
source_review: {"scope":"Zenodo v1 exact-certificate deposit and metadata; Infinity Machine §3.2 and Appendix A.1; prior certified bound","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Language-model safety probes transferred despite shifts in learned directions
summary: Across four language-model families, the directions fitted to separate benign and harmful requests shifted by about 17° to 35° after distillation or instruction tuning. Applying the base probes unchanged shifted AUC by −0.011 to +0.027 on XSTest and −0.015 to +0.053 on an independent prompt set.
ai_technology: Fitted linear activation probes; Qwen2.5, Llama 3.1 and distilled DeepSeek-R1 variants
organization: Independent researcher Marios Tsatsos
tested: Linear classifiers trained on the four base models were evaluated unchanged on two matched successors per family. Transfer was compared with the same probe’s performance on the base model.
unknown: Similar observed accuracy does not establish equivalence, and XSTest fold intervals are too narrow. On OR-Bench the probes flagged 29% to 42% of benign prompts that sounded harmful.
ai_role: Fitted activation classifiers estimated directions and classification performance on base and successor models. Their transfer separated change in direction from change in discrimination.
source_review: {"scope":"§§3–6, Appendix B and front matter","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Claude Fable produced a quadratic-query algorithm for a hidden cycle problem
summary: Claude Fable 5.1 designed a solver for CycleUncover, a black-box problem that hides an even cycle in a bitstring fitness function. The solver reconstructs a two-coloring from fitness queries. Lean checked the expected O(n²) query bound, while the paper proves an exponential bound for the classical (1+1) evolutionary algorithm on this problem.
ai_technology: Claude Fable 5.1; staged algorithm design and Lean proof generation
organization: University of Birmingham
tested: The authors defined the hidden-cycle oracle and supplied a staged formal framework. Their report gives a Lean-checked bound for the generated algorithm and a separate lower-bound argument for the comparator.
unknown: This result concerns one constructed oracle family. It neither establishes that the bound is optimal nor demonstrates empirical speed or general maximum independent-set efficiency.
ai_role: Claude Fable proposed the oracle-query solver and produced the formal expected-query proof under the supplied framework.
source_review: {"scope":"§5.2/Theorem 5.1, Table 2, Appendices E and F.7 and front matter","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Distilled equations predicted instability in simulated multi-planet systems
summary: Researchers distilled a neural network trained on three-planet simulations into compact equations for orbital instability time. Tested on previously simulated five-planet systems, the equations captured changes of orders of magnitude near strong orbital resonances. A systematic error remained for closely spaced planets.
ai_technology: Sparse neural feature learning; PySR symbolic regression
organization: Cornell University; MIT; Harvey Mudd College; University of Cambridge
tested: The equation used sparse statistics from short numerical integrations. It was tested on held-out three-planet simulations and on an existing five-planet grid under a neighboring-trio approximation.
unknown: The five-planet grid used equal masses and circular coplanar orbits. Results are approximate predictions of simulated dynamics, with compressed prediction ranges and no observational validation.
ai_role: The network learned sparse combinations of orbital elements. PySR converted its predicted instability times into closed-form expressions over those learned variables.
source_review: {"scope":"Model equations, Results, Figures 2–4, Appendices A–C and physical interpretation","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Newly appearing links concentrated around hubs in three news narratives
summary: In language-model maps of coverage of three news events, 44% to 51% of next-day emerging links touched an entity in the top tenth by network degree. A ranking based on endpoint degree beat a historical-link baseline on these emerging links, and the margin shrank when high-degree entities were removed.
ai_technology: Claude Haiku, GPT-4.1 and Gemini semantic edge extraction
organization: Arizona State University
tested: The retrospective comparison covered the Canadian Freedom Convoy, Hurricane Melissa and the 2025–26 Iranian protests. It used rolling windows and three separate language-model extractors.
unknown: The graphs use model-extracted relations without human gold labels. Candidate negatives were sampled randomly, favoring degree-based rankings. The result describes links represented in coverage of three events.
ai_role: Language models resolved references and extracted semantic relations from each article, which supplied the networks used to quantify where next-day links appeared.
source_review: {"scope":"§§3–5, Figures 8–9 and front matter","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: A confidence probe rose on repeated wrong answers in Qwen2.5
summary: A probe trained to read answer correctness from first-turn activations gave higher scores when Qwen2.5-7B repeated an incorrect answer. On questions held out from probe training, scores rose by about 0.32 after either a re-ask or agreement. Other confidence measures disagreed, and the pattern did not reproduce consistently across tested models.
ai_technology: Qwen2.5-7B and other language models; fitted linear activation probe
organization: Hanoi University of Science and Technology
tested: A frozen first-turn probe was compared against three other confidence measures. The post hoc check refitted the probe in five folds grouped by question and compared it with probes fit to shuffled labels.
unknown: The strongest result concerns short-answer tasks in Qwen2.5-7B. A cleaned Llama-3 analysis provided support; four other models failed to reproduce the pattern consistently. Probe scores do not directly measure belief.
ai_role: The fitted linear readout made it possible to compare answer-related signals from learned model activations with confidence estimates from the same dialogue.
source_review: {"scope":"§§3 and 5–8, held-out grouped analysis, and front matter","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Pose errors became easier to read after two vision models fused their views
summary: On 903 valid difficult image pairs, linear probes distinguished VGGT pose errors with an AUC of 0.935 from its late features and about 0.65 from its per-image encoder. A second reconstruction model showed a similar layer pattern. The signal emerged after the networks began combining information across views.
ai_technology: VGGT; π³; fitted linear activation probes
organization: University of Wisconsin-Madison; Chalmers University of Technology
tested: The probes used frozen activation features and category-held-out evaluation, with shuffled-label and image-size controls. The authors also compared predictions with confidence outputs and tested transfer to other datasets.
unknown: The pairs were deliberately hard and the failure signal varied with dataset and rotation versus translation errors. Layer profiles show decodable information; they do not establish the causal computation or improvements in multi-view reconstruction.
ai_role: Linear predictors fitted to features at successive layers measured where information about pose failure became available.
source_review: {"scope":"§§3–5, Figure 3 and Tables 3–4","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Vision models often encoded the same concept change differently across contexts
summary: Across 46 vision encoders, the direction for a change such as dry to wet was detectable within individual visual contexts much more often than across them: 97.8% versus 18.3% of the compared cases in that example. The contrast varied substantially by concept.
ai_technology: Pretrained vision encoders including ViT; learned embedding representations and fitted probes
organization: University of Tübingen; KAIST
tested: The authors matched image embeddings for ten concept families, then compared within-context and cross-context direction consistency against random baselines. They also tested linear probe transfer across contexts.
unknown: Matching approximates changes in one concept using images that may differ in other ways. Detection rates depend on the chosen concepts, contexts, models, direction metric and statistical controls.
ai_role: Learned vision embeddings supplied concept-transition vectors for within- and cross-context tests, and fitted probes tested whether aligned directions predicted transfer.
source_review: {"scope":"§§3–5, Table 1 and probe-transfer analysis","date":"2026-11-21"}

title: Two model-screened magnesium alloy routes passed tensile tests
summary: A model-screened magnesium alloy containing gadolinium and yttrium reached 296 MPa yield strength and 398 MPa tensile strength in lab tests. A separate route using recycled feedstock produced AZ31 with similar mechanical properties to its primary-feedstock comparison. The study estimated 40.4% lower operating costs and 88.9% lower emissions for that route.
ai_technology: Physics-informed ensemble of random forests and XGBoost
organization: Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Max Planck Institute for Sustainable Materials

organization: University of Massachusetts Lowell; Bedford VA Healthcare System
tested: The reanalysis used 38 control and22 Alzheimer-labeled samples, with82 protein measurements generating6,642 ordered ratios. Leave-one-out scores informed selection of best subsets; observed selected-ratio differences were then examined in the same samples.
unknown: Feature search and hyperparameter selection reused the LOOCV results, so headline98–100percent separation is selection-informed and not a new independent test. summary: In 864,339 registry patients with atrial fibrillation, an enhanced XGBoost model identified documented anticoagulant prescriptions with a test AUROC of0.811. organization: Stanford University; American College of Cardiology

Concurrent medications and INR can reflect prescribing or monitoring consequences rather than causes; same-clinic records can occur on both sides of the random split. Missing fields and voluntary outpatient practices limit representativeness. The CHA2DS2-VASc comparator is a clinical stroke-risk score, not a prescription model; no causal disparity, guideline benefit or improved treatment outcome is established.

summary: Missing-data-resilient machine-learning pipelines, including gradient boosting and a tabular foundation model, forecast acute food crisis occurrence 3, 6 and 9 months ahead across 80 countries using monthly subnational data for 2007-2024, exceeding no-skill baselines by 15 to 50 percentage points in PR-AUC under nested cross-validation. Internal AUROC was 0.91, and six external sets across US hospitals and a Brazilian cohort gave AUROCs of 0.90-0.95. title: Machine learning identifies GATA factors coordinating Arabidopsis root development

It yielded a memory-two bilateral reciprocity (MTBR) strategy that outperforms a wide range of strategies in pairwise interactions with high payoffs. In evolving populations MTBR is reported to dominate and to foster higher cooperation and social welfare in homogeneous and heterogeneous structures and across game types, verified by simulations and mathematical analysis. The result is theoretical and simulated, with no empirical human data.
